The graph. Which milestone runs, the token budget, the error boundary, and the hand-off to the next run — and nothing else. The single-workflow contract is about one launchable graph, not one physical file.

1/** @jsxImportSource smithers-orchestrator */
2/**
3 * Operation Ferric — the single durable Smithers workflow.
4 *
5 * Rewrites React's runtime in Rust (WASM in the browser, native for SSR), judged
6 * by React's own unmodified test suite. Spec: .smithers/specs/react-rust-port.md
7 * (v3) plus the round-3 gate-DAG spec text.
8 *
9 * This file is the GRAPH. It holds no prompts and no component bodies:
10 * - prompts live in .smithers/prompts/ferric-*.mdx
11 * - components live in .smithers/components/ferric/*.tsx
12 * The single-script contract (spec §6) is about one workflow — one launchable
13 * graph, no Subflow and no second workflow — not about one physical file.
14 *
15 * Launch contract (M0 only, detached, FROM THE CAMPAIGN REPO ROOT):
16 * cd <campaignRepo> && smithers up .smithers/workflows/react-rust-port.tsx -d
17 * The foundation gate hard-fails if the launch root is not the campaign repo:
18 * worktree lanes fork the launch root while landings merge into the campaign
19 * repo, so they must be the same repository.
20 */
21import { Aspects, ContinueAsNew, Sequence, TryCatchFinally, UI } from "smithers-orchestrator";
22import { Workflow, Task, smithers, outputs } from "../components/ferric/ferricSmithers";
23import { FoundationAndBudget } from "../components/ferric/FoundationAndBudget";
24import { PhaseM0 } from "../components/ferric/PhaseM0";
25import { PhaseM25 } from "../components/ferric/PhaseM25";
26import { PhaseM3 } from "../components/ferric/PhaseM3";
27import { PhaseM4 } from "../components/ferric/PhaseM4";
28import { PhaseM5M6 } from "../components/ferric/PhaseM5M6";
29import { PhaseM7 } from "../components/ferric/PhaseM7";
30import { PhaseM8 } from "../components/ferric/PhaseM8";
31import { PhaseGA } from "../components/ferric/PhaseGA";
32import { PhaseM9 } from "../components/ferric/PhaseM9";
33import { TrialPhase } from "../components/ferric/TrialPhase";
34import { SuiteTask } from "../components/ferric/SuiteTask";
35import { Sidecar } from "smithers-orchestrator";
36import { schemaAdherenceScorer, latencyScorer } from "smithers-orchestrator/scorers";
37import { luna, terra } from "../components/ferric/ferricAgents";
38import { MILESTONE_TOKEN_BUDGET, cfg, type SliceDef } from "../components/ferric/ferricConfig";
39import M1FlagCodegenPrompt from "../prompts/ferric-m1-flag-codegen.mdx";
40
41const M1_SLICES: SliceDef[] = [
42 { id: "m1-react-is", kind: "phase", modules: ["react-is"], gate: "react-is jest suite, 100%" },
43 { id: "m1-shared", kind: "phase", modules: ["shared"], gate: "shared jest suite, 100%" },
44];
45const M2_SLICES: SliceDef[] = [
46 {
47 id: "m2-scheduler",
48 kind: "phase",
49 modules: ["scheduler"],
50 gate: "Scheduler suite 100% incl. unstable_mock exports",
51 },
52 {
53 id: "m2-noop-skeleton",
54 kind: "phase",
55 modules: ["react-noop-renderer skeleton"],
56 gate: "noop host mounts/schedules/commits through Ferric",
57 },
58];
59
60export default smithers((ctx) => {
61 const c = cfg(ctx);
62 const m = c.milestone;
63
64 const phase =
65 m === "M0" ? (
66 <PhaseM0 ctx={ctx} c={c} />
67 ) : m === "M1" ? (
68 <TrialPhase
69 ctx={ctx}
70 c={c}
71 milestone="M1"
72 slices={M1_SLICES}
73 gateId="gate-m1-exit"
74 summary="The trial exists to prove the machine — implement, two adversarial reviews, deterministic verify, land, ratchet — on 4.2k lines before it carries the reconciler."
75 extra={
76 <Sidecar
77 id="m1:flag-codegen"
78 agent={terra}
79 sidecar={luna}
80 output={outputs.frcSlice}
81 sidecarOutput={outputs.frcSidecarShadow}
82 scorers={{
83 schema: { scorer: schemaAdherenceScorer() },
84 latency: { scorer: latencyScorer({ targetMs: 1_800_000, maxMs: 3_600_000 }) },
85 }}
86 >
87 <M1FlagCodegenPrompt repo={c.repo} reactRepo={c.reactRepo} />
88 </Sidecar>
89 }
90 />
91 ) : m === "M2" ? (
92 <TrialPhase
93 ctx={ctx}
94 c={c}
95 milestone="M2"
96 slices={M2_SLICES}
97 gateId="gate-m2-exit"
98 summary="M2 does not close on the scheduler suite alone: the WHOLE remaining React suite must stay green while running on the Rust scheduler through the swappable JavaScript seam (D2)."
99 evidence={
100 <SuiteTask
101 id="m2:seam-suite"
102 leg="whole suite on Rust unstable_mock through the require('scheduler') seam"
103 args={["--leg", "scheduler-seam"]}
104 repo={c.repo}
105 />
106 }
107 />
108 ) : m === "M25" ? (
109 <PhaseM25 ctx={ctx} c={c} />
110 ) : m === "M3" ? (
111 <PhaseM3 ctx={ctx} c={c} />
112 ) : m === "M4" ? (
113 <PhaseM4 ctx={ctx} c={c} />
114 ) : m === "M5M6" ? (
115 <PhaseM5M6 ctx={ctx} c={c} />
116 ) : m === "M7" ? (
117 <PhaseM7 ctx={ctx} c={c} />
118 ) : m === "M8" ? (
119 <PhaseM8 ctx={ctx} c={c} />
120 ) : m === "GA" ? (
121 <PhaseGA ctx={ctx} c={c} />
122 ) : m === "M9" ? (
123 <PhaseM9 ctx={ctx} c={c} />
124 ) : (
125 <Task id="campaign-complete" output={outputs.frcCloseout}>
126 {{
127 milestone: "DONE",
128 summaryMarkdown: `Operation Ferric complete. Lineage: ${[...c.lineage, "final"].join(" → ")}. Every gate was human-decided; the ratchet stayed monotone end to end; publishes were idempotency-keyed and last in the graph.`,
129 killed: false,
130 }}
131 </Task>
132 );
133
134 return (
135 <Workflow name="react-rust-port">
136 <UI entry="../ui/react-rust-port.tsx" />
137 <Sequence>
138 <FoundationAndBudget ctx={ctx} c={c} />
139 <TryCatchFinally
140 id={`ferric-${m}`}
141 try={<Aspects tokenBudget={{ max: MILESTONE_TOKEN_BUDGET, onExceeded: "fail" }}>{phase}</Aspects>}
142 // Scoped to exactly ONE code: token-budget exhaustion rolls this
143 // milestone into a fresh run (a durable /clear — the engine carries
144 // completed output rows across, so nothing re-runs). Every other
145 // failure, including a deliberate gate denial, stops loudly. An
146 // earlier draft caught everything here and turned denials into an
147 // infinite, self-funding loop.
148 catchErrors={["ASPECT_BUDGET_EXCEEDED"]}
149 catch={
150 <ContinueAsNew state={{ milestone: m, spentCents: c.spentCents, lineage: [...c.lineage, ctx.runId] }} />
151 }
152 />
153 </Sequence>
154 </Workflow>
155 );
156});

1/** @jsxImportSource react */
2/**
3 * Operation Ferric — slice code-review surface (companion to react-rust-port.tsx).
4 *
5 * A reviewer picks a slice node in the run tree and gets the whole review story
6 * in one place: the implementer's report, both adversarial reviews, the
7 * deterministic verifier's verdict, the landing/ratchet row, the node's LIVE
8 * agent chat, and the pending human gates — every widget a shipped
9 * smithers-orchestrator component over the gateway-react hooks.
10 *
11 * Diffs render through the house DiffHunks anatomy via parseUnifiedFile, fed
12 * from the verify row (vcs.tsx reference-bundle pattern: diff text travels as a
13 * node-output field). The Ferric verifier stores its `jj diff --stat` in
14 * `reasons`; persist the full patch on the verify row (a `diffText` field) to
15 * light the full hunk view up.
16 *
17 * Open it by pointing the workflow's <UI entry> here, or register it on a
18 * gateway: gateway.register("react-rust-port", wf, { ui: { entry: ".smithers/ui/react-rust-port-review.tsx" } })
19 */
20import { useState } from "react";
21import { createGatewayReactRoot, useGatewayNodeOutput } from "smithers-orchestrator/gateway-react";
22import {
23 ConnectionBadge,
24 GatewayApprovalList,
25 MonitorButton,
26 NodeChatStream,
27 RunList,
28 RunMeta,
29 RunTree,
30 StatusPill,
31 WorkflowUiShell,
32} from "smithers-orchestrator/gateway-ui";
33import { DiffHunks, EmptyState, KpiStat, parseUnifiedFile } from "smithers-orchestrator/ui";
34
35const WORKFLOW = "react-rust-port";
36const SLICE_NODE = /^(?<slice>.+?):(implement|review-claude|review-codex|verify|land.*)$/;
37
38function initialRunId(): string | undefined {
39 return new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).get("runId") ?? undefined;
40}
41
42/** One persisted row, unwrapped defensively (`data.row`, booleans as 0/1). */
43function useRow(runId: string | undefined, nodeId: string | undefined) {
44 const out = useGatewayNodeOutput({ runId, nodeId, iteration: 0 });
45 const row = (out.data as any)?.row ?? null;
46 return { row, status: String((out.data as any)?.status ?? "pending") };
47}
48
49function RowCard(props: { title: string; ok?: boolean | null; children: React.ReactNode }) {
50 return (
51 <section style={{ display: "grid", gap: 6 }}>
52 <header style={{ display: "flex", alignItems: "center", gap: 8 }}>
53 <strong style={{ fontSize: 13 }}>{props.title}</strong>
54 {props.ok != null ? <StatusPill status={props.ok ? "ok" : "blocked"} /> : <StatusPill status="pending" />}
55 </header>
56 {props.children}
57 </section>
58 );
59}
60
61function SliceReview({ runId, sliceId }: { runId?: string; sliceId: string }) {
62 const impl = useRow(runId, `${sliceId}:implement`);
63 const revA = useRow(runId, `${sliceId}:review-claude`);
64 const revB = useRow(runId, `${sliceId}:review-codex`);
65 const verify = useRow(runId, `${sliceId}:verify`);
66 const truthy = (v: unknown) => v === true || v === 1;
67 const diffText: string = String(verify.row?.diffText ?? "");
68 return (
69 <div style={{ display: "grid", gap: 14 }}>
70 <div style={{ display: "grid", gridTemplateColumns: "repeat(3, 1fr)", gap: 10 }}>
71 <KpiStat label="Slice" value={sliceId} />
72 <KpiStat
73 label="Verifier"
74 value={verify.row ? (truthy(verify.row.ok) ? "green" : "VETO") : "pending"}
75 hint={verify.row ? `${verify.row.testsPassed}/${verify.row.testsTotal} tests` : "deterministic, in-lane"}
76 />
77 <KpiStat
78 label="Reviews"
79 value={`${[revA, revB].filter((r) => truthy(r.row?.approved)).length}/2 approved`}
80 hint="opus + opposite-codex, diff-only"
81 />
82 </div>
83
84 {diffText ? (
85 <DiffHunks file={parseUnifiedFile(diffText)} />
86 ) : (
87 <EmptyState
88 title="No patch text on the verify row"
89 description={`The verifier stored: ${String(verify.row?.reasons ?? "…nothing yet")}. Persist the lane patch as frcVerify.diffText to render full hunks here.`}
90 />
91 )}
92
93 <RowCard
94 title="Implementer report"
95 ok={impl.row ? truthy(impl.row.cargoCheckOk) && truthy(impl.row.testsOk) : null}
96 >
97 <p style={{ margin: 0, fontSize: 13 }}>{String(impl.row?.summary ?? "not yet reported")}</p>
98 </RowCard>
99 <RowCard title="Adversarial review — claude-opus" ok={revA.row ? truthy(revA.row.approved) : null}>
100 <p style={{ margin: 0, fontSize: 13, whiteSpace: "pre-wrap" }}>{String(revA.row?.findings ?? "…")}</p>
101 </RowCard>
102 <RowCard title="Adversarial review — codex (opposite tier)" ok={revB.row ? truthy(revB.row.approved) : null}>
103 <p style={{ margin: 0, fontSize: 13, whiteSpace: "pre-wrap" }}>{String(revB.row?.findings ?? "…")}</p>
104 </RowCard>
105 <RowCard title="Deterministic verifier (the veto)" ok={verify.row ? truthy(verify.row.ok) : null}>
106 <p style={{ margin: 0, fontSize: 13, whiteSpace: "pre-wrap" }}>{String(verify.row?.reasons ?? "…")}</p>
107 </RowCard>
108
109 {/* Live agent feedback for the seat under review. */}
110 <NodeChatStream
111 runId={runId}
112 nodeId={`${sliceId}:implement`}
113 title={`${sliceId} — implementer, live`}
114 height={320}
115 />
116 </div>
117 );
118}
119
120function App() {
121 const [runId, setRunId] = useState<string | undefined>(initialRunId());
122 const [sliceId, setSliceId] = useState<string | undefined>(undefined);
123
124 return (
125 <WorkflowUiShell
126 title="Ferric slice review"
127 meta={<RunMeta runId={runId} showConnection={false} />}
128 actions={
129 <div style={{ display: "flex", alignItems: "center", gap: 12 }}>
130 <ConnectionBadge />
131 <MonitorButton runId={runId} />
132 </div>
133 }
134 >
135 <div style={{ display: "grid", gridTemplateColumns: "240px 300px 1fr", gap: 12, padding: 16 }}>
136 <RunList
137 filter={{ workflow: WORKFLOW, limit: 20 }}
138 activeRunId={runId}
139 onSelect={(id: string) => {
140 setRunId(id);
141 setSliceId(undefined);
142 }}
143 />
144 <RunTree
145 runId={runId}
146 onSelectNode={(node: { id: string }) => {
147 const m = SLICE_NODE.exec(node.id);
148 if (m?.groups?.slice) setSliceId(m.groups.slice);
149 }}
150 />
151 <div style={{ display: "grid", gap: 14, alignContent: "start" }}>
152 {/* The human gates this reviewer can clear, right where the evidence is. */}
153 <GatewayApprovalList filter={{ workflow: WORKFLOW }} note />
154 {sliceId ? (
155 <SliceReview runId={runId} sliceId={sliceId} />
156 ) : (
157 <EmptyState
158 title="Pick a slice"
159 description="Select any slice node (implement / review / verify / land) in the run tree to open its full review story."
160 />
161 )}
162 </div>
163 </div>
164 </WorkflowUiShell>
165 );
166}

168createGatewayReactRoot(<App />);

1/** @jsxImportSource smithers-orchestrator */
2import { Task, outputs } from "./ferricSmithers";
3import { assertNotInfra, sh } from "./ferricShell";
4
5/**
6 * One benchmark cell, judged against the contract frozen at M0.
7 *
8 * The pass predicate is supplied by the caller because the thresholds differ per
9 * workload (client update ops cap at 1.10x; SSR has a 0.95x floor). A missing
10 * ratio is -1, which fails every predicate rather than defaulting to success.
11 */
12export function BenchTask(props: { id: string; bench: string; pass: (ratioX1000: number) => boolean; repo: string }) {
13 return (
14 <Task id={props.id} output={outputs.frcBench} retries={2}>
15 {async () => {
16 const r = await sh(["bash", "scripts/ferric/bench.sh", props.bench], props.repo);
17 assertNotInfra(r, props.id);
18 const m = /RATIO_X1000=(\d+)/.exec(r.out);
19 const ratio = m ? Number(m[1]) : -1;
20 return {
21 bench: props.bench,
22 ratioX1000: ratio,
23 withinContract: m != null && props.pass(ratio),
24 };
25 }}
26 </Task>
27 );
28}

55 lines 2.0 KB

The only Approval mount in the campaign. Every human decision routes through here, which is what makes “no gate auto-approves” checkable at runtime.

1/** @jsxImportSource smithers-orchestrator */
2import { Approval } from "smithers-orchestrator";
3import { outputs } from "./ferricSmithers";
4import { APPROVAL_SLA, GATE_REGISTRY, type FerricGateId } from "./ferricGates";
5
6/**
7 * Resolve a gate's durable node id.
8 *
9 * `instance` exists for gates that can legitimately fire more than once in a
10 * campaign. An approval row is keyed by (run, node, iteration), so a gate with a
11 * STATIC id is answered exactly once and every later occurrence reads that same
12 * stored `approved: true` — a one-shot approval silently becomes a perpetual
13 * auto-pass. That defeats the flagship "no gate auto-approves" invariant, and it
14 * bit the ratchet-halt gate: clearing one regression cleared every future one.
15 */
16export const gateNodeId = (id: FerricGateId, instance?: string | number) =>
17 instance === undefined ? id : `${id}:${instance}`;
18
19/**
20 * The ONLY `Approval` mount in the campaign.
21 *
22 * The foundation task greps every campaign source file at runtime and fails the
23 * run if a second approval site or any auto-approve option ever appears, so this
24 * component is the enforcement point for "every gate is human".
25 */
26export function CampaignGate(props: {
27 id: FerricGateId;
28 summary: string;
29 /** Distinguishes repeat firings of a re-armable gate (e.g. a halt epoch). */
30 instance?: string | number;
31}) {
32 const reg = GATE_REGISTRY[props.id];
33 return (
34 <Approval
35 id={gateNodeId(props.id, props.instance)}
36 output={outputs.frcGate}
37 onDeny={reg.onDeny}
38 request={{
39 title: reg.title,
40 summary: props.summary,
41 metadata: {
42 sla: APPROVAL_SLA,
43 neverAutoApprove: true,
44 gateId: props.id,
45 ...(props.instance === undefined ? {} : { instance: String(props.instance) }),
46 },
47 }}
48 />
49 );
50}
51
52/** Read a gate's persisted decision, or undefined while it is still pending. */
53export const gateRow = (ctx: any, id: FerricGateId, instance?: string | number) =>
54 ctx.outputMaybe(outputs.frcGate, { nodeId: gateNodeId(id, instance) });

1/** @jsxImportSource smithers-orchestrator */
2import { existsSync, readFileSync, readdirSync, realpathSync } from "node:fs";
3import { join } from "node:path";
4import { Sequence } from "smithers-orchestrator";
5import { Task, outputs } from "./ferricSmithers";
6import { CampaignGate, gateRow } from "./CampaignGate";
7import { Closeout } from "./Closeout";
8import { LAUNCH_ROOT, MODEL_CAP_CENTS, PRE_M8_STOP_CENTS, type FerricConfig } from "./ferricConfig";
9import { SCRIPTS } from "./ferricShell";
10import { RefreshAccountUsage } from "../accounts/RefreshAccountUsage";
11
12/** The workflow's own source, for the runtime self-audit. */
13const WORKFLOW_SOURCE = join(LAUNCH_ROOT, ".smithers/workflows/react-rust-port.tsx");
14const COMPONENT_DIR = join(LAUNCH_ROOT, ".smithers/components/ferric");
15
16/**
17 * Every campaign source file the self-audit must read.
18 *
19 * Auditing only the workflow and CampaignGate covered 2 of 19 JSX-bearing files:
20 * a second `<Approval>` dropped into any Phase*.tsx, Slice.tsx or
21 * PublishPipeline.tsx passed undetected while the audit still reported
22 * selfAuditOk. Splitting the campaign across files created that blind spot, so
23 * the audit enumerates the directory rather than a hand-listed pair.
24 */
25function campaignSources(): string[] {
26 const files = [WORKFLOW_SOURCE];
27 try {
28 for (const f of readdirSync(COMPONENT_DIR)) {
29 if (f.endsWith(".tsx") || f.endsWith(".ts")) files.push(join(COMPONENT_DIR, f));
30 }
31 } catch {
32 /* directory missing is caught by the existence checks below */
33 }
34 return files;
35}
36
37/**
38 * Everything that must be true before a single token is spent, plus the budget
39 * admission decision for this run.
40 *
41 * The identity checks exist because three independent blind implementations of
42 * this workflow died on the same two bugs: worktree lanes forking one repository
43 * while landings merged into another, and a "deterministic" layer that called
44 * scripts nothing ever created.
45 */
46export function FoundationAndBudget({ ctx, c }: { ctx: any; c: FerricConfig }) {
47 const budget = ctx.outputMaybe(outputs.frcBudget, { nodeId: "budget" });
48 const expansionApproved = gateRow(ctx, "gate-budget-expand")?.approved === true;
49 // Depends on the level alone, never on admitNewWork: an audited version gated
50 // this on the very flag that goes false when the gate becomes necessary, so
51 // the campaign stalled at 90% with no gate and no lifeline.
52 const needExpansion = budget != null && budget.levelPctX100 >= 9000 && !expansionApproved;
53 // A blocked budget must TERMINATE, not stall. When admission is off and no
54 // expansion decision can still change that (hard cap, the pre-M8 stop line, or
55 // an expansion the operator denied), the campaign publishes its signed closeout
56 // instead of rendering nothing forever with no gate and no lifeline.
57 const budgetTerminal =
58 budget != null &&
59 budget.admitNewWork === false &&
60 (budget.levelPctX100 >= 10000 ||
61 budget.spentCents >= PRE_M8_STOP_CENTS ||
62 gateRow(ctx, "gate-budget-expand")?.approved === false);
63
64 return (
65 <Sequence label="foundation">
66 {/* Snapshot live per-account headroom BEFORE any seat is chosen. Render is
67 synchronous and cannot probe the network, so selection reads this
68 task's file; without it the fleet ordering is whatever was true when
69 the snapshot was last written. */}
70 <RefreshAccountUsage output={outputs.frcAccounts} />
71 <Task id="foundation" output={outputs.frcFoundation} retries={0}>
72 {async () => {
73 const problems: string[] = [];
74
75 const launchRootOk = realpathSync(LAUNCH_ROOT) === realpathSync(c.repo);
76 if (!launchRootOk) {
77 problems.push(
78 `launch root ${LAUNCH_ROOT} != campaign repo ${c.repo} — worktree lanes would fork the wrong repository. Launch from the campaign repo root.`,
79 );
80 }
81 if (!existsSync(join(c.repo, ".jj")) && !existsSync(join(c.repo, ".git"))) {
82 problems.push(`${c.repo} is not a jj/git repository`);
83 }
84
85 const scriptsOk = SCRIPTS.every((s) => existsSync(join(c.repo, s)));
86 if (c.milestone !== "M0" && !scriptsOk) {
87 problems.push(`missing deterministic scripts (${SCRIPTS.join(", ")}) — M0 authors them; do not skip M0`);
88 }
89
90 const queueOk = existsSync(c.queuePath);
91 if (!queueOk) problems.push(`MODULE_QUEUE.tsv not found at ${c.queuePath}`);
92
93 // Self-audit: exactly one Approval mount in the campaign, and no
94 // auto-approve anywhere. Makes "every gate is human" checkable.
95 let selfAuditOk = true;
96 const auditFiles = campaignSources().filter((f) => existsSync(f));
97 if (auditFiles.length > 1) {
98 // Count real JSX mounts, not prose: a comment mentioning the
99 // component (including the one above) must not trip the audit, or
100 // the check becomes a game of avoiding words in documentation.
101 const codeLines = auditFiles
102 .flatMap((f) => readFileSync(f, "utf8").split("\n"))
103 .filter((line) => {
104 const t = line.trim();
105 return !t.startsWith("*") && !t.startsWith("//") && !t.startsWith("/*");
106 });
107 const approvalMounts = codeLines.filter((l) => /<Approval(\s|\/|>|$)/.test(l)).length;
108 const autoApprovals = codeLines.filter((l) => /autoApprove\s*=/.test(l)).length;
109 selfAuditOk = approvalMounts === 1 && autoApprovals === 0;
110 if (!selfAuditOk) {
111 problems.push(
112 `self-audit failed across ${auditFiles.length} campaign files: ${approvalMounts} Approval mounts (want exactly 1, inside CampaignGate), ${autoApprovals} autoApprove props (want 0)`,
113 );
114 }
115 }
116
117 if (problems.length > 0) {
118 throw new Error(`FOUNDATION GATE RED:\n- ${problems.join("\n- ")}`);
119 }
120 return { launchRootOk, scriptsOk, queueOk, selfAuditOk, detail: `ok @ ${c.milestone}` };
121 }}
122 </Task>
123
124 <Task id="budget" output={outputs.frcBudget}>
125 {() => {
126 // Graduation: warn at 80%, human gate at 90%, stop admitting at 100%
127 // or at the pre-M8 stop line. Spend itself is operator-attested; what
128 // is mechanical is the consequence.
129 const cap = MODEL_CAP_CENTS;
130 const level = Math.floor((c.spentCents / cap) * 10000);
131 const admitNewWork = level < 10000 && (level < 9000 || expansionApproved) && c.spentCents < PRE_M8_STOP_CENTS;
132 const note =
133 level >= 10000
134 ? "HARD CAP: no new work admitted"
135 : level >= 9000
136 ? expansionApproved
137 ? "≥90%: expansion approved"
138 : "≥90%: awaiting budget-expansion gate"
139 : level >= 8000
140 ? "≥80%: warn"
141 : "within envelope";
142 return {
143 spentCents: c.spentCents,
144 capCents: cap,
145 levelPctX100: level,
146 admitNewWork,
147 note,
148 };
149 }}
150 </Task>
151
152 {budgetTerminal ? (
153 <Closeout
154 ctx={ctx}
155 c={c}
156 reason={`Budget stop: ${budget.note} (attested $${(budget.spentCents / 100).toFixed(0)} against a $${(MODEL_CAP_CENTS / 100).toFixed(0)} cap, level ${(budget.levelPctX100 / 100).toFixed(1)}%). No further work is admitted; the campaign closes out rather than stalling silently.`}
157 />
158 ) : needExpansion ? (
159 <CampaignGate
160 id="gate-budget-expand"
161 summary={`Model spend is at ${(budget.levelPctX100 / 100).toFixed(1)}% of the $${(MODEL_CAP_CENTS / 100 / 1000).toFixed(0)}k cap ($${(budget.spentCents / 100).toFixed(0)} attested). Approve to keep working toward the cap; deny to stop and rescope. Cut order: App Router/edge promotion, then extra beta seats, then the M9 long tail, then native platform breadth. Never cut: the oracle, the backend assertion, byte-identical errors, security response, the release train, rollback, or the owned GA fixtures.`}
162 />
163 ) : null}
164 </Sequence>
165 );
166}

1/** @jsxImportSource smithers-orchestrator */
2import { Task, outputs } from "./ferricSmithers";
3import { assertNotInfra, sh } from "./ferricShell";
4
5/**
6 * Differential fuzzing against upstream React. `clean` requires the full
7 * requested case count AND zero divergences, so a short run cannot pass.
8 */
9export function FuzzTask(props: { id: string; mode: string; cases: number; repo: string }) {
10 return (
11 <Task id={props.id} output={outputs.frcFuzz} retries={2}>
12 {async () => {
13 const r = await sh(["bash", "scripts/ferric/fuzz.sh", props.mode, "--cases", String(props.cases)], props.repo);
14 assertNotInfra(r, props.id);
15 const m = /CASES=(\d+)\s+DIVERGENCES=(\d+)/.exec(r.out);
16 return {
17 mode: props.mode,
18 casesRun: m ? Number(m[1]) : 0,
19 divergences: m ? Number(m[2]) : -1,
20 clean: !!m && Number(m[1]) >= props.cases && m[2] === "0",
21 };
22 }}
23 </Task>
24 );
25}

58 );

13/**
14 * M4 — the reconciler, ported through the noop oracle.
15 *
16 * The bulk of the campaign: 22 leaf modules plus six cohorts over the reconciler's
17 * import cycle, judged by 76 files and 1,039 cases. Ends at the week-6 go/no-go.
18 */
19export function PhaseM4({ ctx, c }: { ctx: any; c: FerricConfig }) {
20 const queue = ctx.outputMaybe(outputs.frcQueue, { nodeId: "queue-parse" });
21 const slices: SliceDef[] = queue ? JSON.parse(queue.slices) : [];
22 const f = frontier(ctx, c.repo, slices, outputs);
23 const half = f.total > 0 && f.landed.length >= Math.ceil(f.total / 2);
24 const spendM4 = gateRow(ctx, "gate-spend-m4");
25 const gonogo = gateRow(ctx, "gate-wk6");
26 const gateReady = f.total > 0 && (f.done || f.blocked.length > 0);
27
28 // Deterministic drift check from the durable ledger. The shipped DriftDetector
29 // is single-shot and agent-driven, which is the wrong tool for a frontier that
30 // moves on every landing.
31 const offTrack = f.total > 0 && f.blocked.length >= 2;
32
33 return (
34 <Sequence label="M4 — reconciler via noop oracle">
35 <QueueParse c={c} />
36 {slices.length > 0 ? <PortCampaign ctx={ctx} c={c} phase="M4" slices={slices} /> : null}
37
38 {offTrack ? (
39 <Task id="m4:drift-alert" output={outputs.frcDriftAlert} agent={planner} continueOnFail timeoutMs={1_800_000}>
40 <M4DriftAlertPrompt
41 landed={f.landed.length}
42 total={f.total}
43 blockedCount={f.blocked.length}
44 blockedIds={f.blocked.map((b) => b.id).join(", ")}
45 />
46 </Task>
47 ) : null}
48
49 {half && !spendM4 ? (
50 <CampaignGate
51 id="gate-spend-m4"
52 summary={`Half of the M4 queue has landed (${f.landed.length}/${f.total}). Attested spend $${(c.spentCents / 100).toFixed(0)} against the $${(MODEL_CAP_CENTS / 100).toFixed(0)} cap and the $${(PRE_M8_STOP_CENTS / 100).toFixed(0)} pre-M8 stop-line.`}
53 />
54 ) : null}
55
56 {gateReady ? (
57 <Sequence>
58 <CampaignGate
59 id="gate-wk6"
60 summary={`M4 week-6 go/no-go. ${f.landed.length}/${f.total} slices landed; ratchet ${f.ledger.passingCount}/${f.ledger.totalCount}. DENY publishes a signed closeout.`}
61 />

1/** @jsxImportSource smithers-orchestrator */
2import { Parallel, Sequence } from "smithers-orchestrator";
3import { Task, outputs } from "./ferricSmithers";
4import { CampaignGate, gateRow } from "./CampaignGate";
5import { Slice } from "./Slice";
6import type { FerricConfig, SliceDef } from "./ferricConfig";
7import { readLedger, writeLedger } from "./ferricLedger";
8
9/**
10 * Queue-backfill over a phase's slices.
11 *
12 * Leaves fan out across the lane budget; cohorts land STRICTLY one at a time and
13 * only after every leaf has landed. That ordering is the D5 rule — never per-module
14 * lanes over the reconciler's 59-module import cycle — and it is enforced by the
15 * shape of this graph rather than by asking an agent to be careful.
16 */
17export function PortCampaign(props: { ctx: any; c: FerricConfig; phase: string; slices: SliceDef[] }) {
18 const { ctx, c, phase, slices } = props;
19 const ledger = readLedger(c.repo);
20 const budget = ctx.outputMaybe(outputs.frcBudget, { nodeId: "budget" });
21 const admit = (budget?.admitNewWork ?? true) && !ledger.halted;
22
23 const remaining = slices.filter((s) => !ledger.landed.includes(s.id));
24 const leafs = remaining.filter((s) => s.kind !== "cohort");
25 const cohorts = remaining.filter((s) => s.kind === "cohort");
26 const cohortsReady = slices.filter((s) => s.kind !== "cohort").every((s) => ledger.landed.includes(s.id));
27
28 return (
29 <Sequence label={`${phase} port campaign`}>
30 {ledger.halted ? (
31 // Keyed by halt epoch: each regression is its own decision. A static
32 // id would let the first clearance permanently auto-pass every later halt.
33 <CampaignGate
34 id="gate-ratchet-halt"
35 instance={`e${ledger.haltEpoch}`}
36 summary={`The monotone ratchet went backwards on a landing in ${phase} (halt epoch ${ledger.haltEpoch}). The merge was reverted and the landing queue is durably halted. Evidence: frcLand rows with regression=true, and the ferric-ledger.json passing count. Approving increments the halt epoch and re-admits landing; denying stops the campaign here.`}
37 />
38 ) : null}
39
40 {ledger.halted && gateRow(ctx, "gate-ratchet-halt", `e${ledger.haltEpoch}`)?.approved ? (
41 <Task id={`${phase}:clear-halt:e${ledger.haltEpoch}`} output={outputs.frcFoundation}>
42 {() => {
43 const led = readLedger(c.repo);
44 writeLedger(c.repo, { ...led, halted: false, haltEpoch: led.haltEpoch + 1 });
45 return {
46 launchRootOk: true,
47 scriptsOk: true,
48 queueOk: true,
49 selfAuditOk: true,
50 detail: `halt cleared, epoch ${led.haltEpoch + 1}`,
51 };
52 }}
53 </Task>
54 ) : null}
55
56 {admit ? (
57 <Sequence>
58 <Parallel id={`${phase}:leaf-lanes`} subtreeConcurrency={c.maxLanes}>
59 {leafs.slice(0, c.maxLanes * 2).map((s) => (
60 <Slice key={s.id} ctx={ctx} c={c} slice={s} />
61 ))}
62 </Parallel>
63 {cohortsReady ? cohorts.slice(0, 1).map((s) => <Slice key={s.id} ctx={ctx} c={c} slice={s} />) : null}
64 </Sequence>
65 ) : null}
66 </Sequence>
67 );
68}

22}

24/**
25 * Decide, gate, then act exactly once.
26 *
27 * Publishing is the campaign's only irreversible act, so the agent that decides
28 * never performs it: the decision stays reviewable and replayable, the act is
29 * isolated behind a human gate and keyed so a retry is a no-op. Callers mount
30 * this LAST — it is mutually exclusive with the milestone hand-off.
31 */
32export function PublishPipeline(props: {
33 ctx: any;
34 c: FerricConfig;
35 artifact: string;
36 idPrefix: string;
37 gateId: FerricGateId;
38 instructions: string;
39}) {
40 const { ctx, c } = props;
41 const decision = ctx.outputMaybe(outputs.frcPublishDecision, {
42 nodeId: `${props.idPrefix}:decide`,
43 });
44 const approved = gateRow(ctx, props.gateId)?.approved === true;
45
46 return (
47 <Sequence label={`publish ${props.artifact}`}>
48 <Task id={`${props.idPrefix}:decide`} output={outputs.frcPublishDecision} agent={planner} timeoutMs={3_600_000}>
49 <PublishDecisionPrompt artifact={props.artifact} instructions={props.instructions} />
50 </Task>
51
52 {decision?.shouldPublish ? (
53 <CampaignGate id={props.gateId} summary={`${decision.reason}\n\nIdempotency key: ${decision.idempotencyKey}`} />
54 ) : null}
55
56 {decision?.shouldPublish && approved ? (
57 <Task id={`${props.idPrefix}:act`} output={outputs.frcPublishAct} noRetry>
58 {async () => {
59 const dir = join(c.repo, ".ferric-published");
60 const marker = publishMarkerPath(c.repo, decision.idempotencyKey);
61 if (existsSync(marker)) {
62 return {
63 artifact: props.artifact,
64 published: true,
65 receipt: `idempotent-skip:${decision.idempotencyKey}`,
66 };
67 }
68 const r = await sh(["bash", "scripts/ferric/publish.sh", props.artifact, decision.idempotencyKey], c.repo);
69 if (!r.ok) throw new Error(`publish act failed:\n${(r.err || r.out).slice(-2000)}`);
70 mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
71 writeFileSync(marker, r.out.slice(-2000));
72 return { artifact: props.artifact, published: true, receipt: r.out.slice(-500) };
73 }}
74 </Task>
75 ) : null}
76 </Sequence>
77 );
78}

1/** @jsxImportSource smithers-orchestrator */
2import { existsSync, readFileSync } from "node:fs";

7/**
8 * The eleven cohorts the reconciler's 59-module import cycle lands as.
9 *
10 * This is an explicit table, not a name regex: the regex bucketing it replaces
11 * let `/Transition/` steal three commit-phase ViewTransition modules into the
12 * hooks cohort, hid a 15.8k-LOC cohort behind a clean-looking count check, and
13 * stamped every cohort with the blanket 76-file suite. The assignment below
14 * comes from a greedy feedback-arc-set linearization of the intra-SCC
15 * dependency graph (see poc/cohort-decomp/decompose.mjs), packed into
16 * contiguous spine runs under the bounds below. It cuts cohort-level
17 * back-edges from 190 (regex) to 57.
18 *
19 * Embedded here rather than added as a TSV column on purpose: the D5 contract
20 * is machine-checked code, and the queue TSV is generated data the check is
21 * supposed to distrust. Putting the grouping in the data would let a
22 * regenerated queue rewrite the contract without a code review.
23 */
24const COHORTS: Array<[string, string[]]> = [
25 [
26 "00",
27 [
28 "ReactFiberCacheComponent",
29 "ReactFiberTreeContext",
30 "ReactFiberStack",
31 "ReactFiberLegacyContext",
32 "ReactEventPriorities",
33 "getComponentNameFromFiber",
34 "ReactFiberComponentStack",
35 "ReactCurrentFiber",
36 "ReactCapturedValue",
37 "ReactFiberActivityComponent",
38 ],
39 ],
40 [
41 "01",
42 [
43 "ReactStrictModeWarnings",
44 "ReactFiberErrorLogger",
45 "ReactFiberHydrationDiffs",
46 "ReactFiberDuplicateViewTransitions",
47 "ReactFiberAct",
48 "ReactFiberDevToolsHook",
49 "ReactFiberLane",
50 "ReactFiberSuspenseComponent",
51 "ReactFiberOffscreenComponent",
52 "ReactFiberTreeReflection",
53 ],
54 ],
55 [
56 "02",
57 [
58 "ReactFiberTransitionTypes",
59 "ReactFiberPerformanceTrack",
60 "ReactFiberScope",
61 "ReactProfilerTimer",
62 "ReactFiberAsyncAction",
63 "ReactFiberTracingMarkerComponent",
64 "ReactFiberThenable",
65 "ReactInternalTypes",
66 "ReactFiberViewTransitionComponent",
67 "ReactFiberRootScheduler",
68 ],
69 ],
70 [
71 "03",
72 [
73 "ReactFiberHostContext",
74 "ReactFiberNewContext",
75 "ReactFiberAsyncDispatcher",
76 "ReactFiber",
77 "ReactFiberHydrationContext",
78 "ReactFiberRoot",
79 "ReactFiberShellHydration",
80 "ReactFiberSuspenseContext",
81 "ReactFiberHiddenContext",
82 "ReactFiberGestureScheduler",
83 ],
84 ],
85 [
86 "04",
87 [
88 "ReactFiberTransition",

90 "ReactChildFiber",
91 "ReactFiberCommitViewTransitions",
92 "ReactFiberCompleteWork",
93 ],
94 ],
95 [
96 "05",
97 [
98 "ReactFiberCommitHostEffects",
99 "ReactFiberClassUpdateQueue",
100 "ReactFiberClassComponent",
101 "ReactFiberConcurrentUpdates",
102 "ReactFiberHotReloading",
103 "ReactFiberCallUserSpace",
104 "ReactFiberThrow",
105 ],
106 ],
107 ["06", ["ReactFiberHooks", "ReactFiberReconciler"]],
108 ["07", ["ReactFiberBeginWork", "ReactFiberCommitEffects"]],
109 ["08", ["ReactFiberCommitWork"]],
110 ["09", ["ReactFiberWorkLoop"]],
111 ["10", ["ReactFiberApplyGesture"]],
112];

114/**
115 * Hard bounds per cohort. MAX_LOC is the top of the ~4-6k smart zone one agent
116 * converges in four implement/review rounds; it must also clear the largest
117 * single module (ReactFiberWorkLoop, 5,246 LOC), which cannot be split.
118 * MAX_MODULES bounds the review surface per round.
119 */
120const MAX_COHORT_LOC = 6000;
121const MAX_COHORT_MODULES = 10;
122
123/** The gate the old component stamped on every cohort. Never acceptable. */
124const BLANKET_GATE = "noop-host reconciler suites (76 files / 1,039 cases)";
125
126const TEST_DIR = (reactRepo: string) => join(reactRepo, "packages", "react-reconciler", "src", "__tests__");
127const SAFE_ID = /^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$/;
128
129const failQueueContract: (why: string) => never = (why) => {
130 throw new Error(
131 `D5_QUEUE_CONTRACT: ${why}. Regenerate MODULE_QUEUE.tsv (report-fable §4.4) or amend the COHORTS table in QueueParse.tsx.`,
132 );
133};
134
135export function parseQueueRows(raw: string) {
136 return raw
137 .trim()
138 .split("\n")
139 .slice(1)
140 .map((l) => {
141 const [order, module_, loc, _fanIn, scc, deps, gating] = l.split("\t");
142 if (!module_ || !SAFE_ID.test(module_)) {
143 failQueueContract(`module id "${module_ ?? ""}" must match ${SAFE_ID}`);
144 }
145 return {
146 order: Number(order),
147 module: module_,
148 loc: Number(loc),
149 scc: (scc ?? "-").trim(),
150 deps: (deps ?? "").trim() ? (deps ?? "").trim().split(",") : [],
151 gate: (gating ?? "").trim(),
152 };
153 });
154}
155
156/** Parse the gating_tests column: `File-test.js(N),...` -> [{file, cases}]. */
157const parseGating = (raw: string): Array<{ file: string; cases: number }> =>
158 !raw
159 ? []
160 : raw.split(",").map((t) => {
161 const m = /^(.+)\((\d+)\)$/.exec(t.trim());
162 return m ? { file: m[1], cases: Number(m[2]) } : { file: t.trim(), cases: 0 };
163 });
164
165/**
166 * Parse MODULE_QUEUE.tsv into landable work, and refuse a queue whose
167 * decomposition is wrong — semantically, not just in shape.
168 *
169 * The D5 contract is a machine check, not advice. The old check verified only
170 * counts (22 leaves, 59 SCC rows, 59 regex matches); this one verifies the
171 * decomposition itself: every SCC module assigned exactly once, every cohort
172 * non-empty and inside the size/LOC bounds, every cohort gated on real test
173 * files that exist in the pinned react checkout, leaves exactly the 22
174 * scc==="-" rows in order, and no cohort gated on the blanket suite.
175 */
176export function QueueParse({ c }: { c: FerricConfig }) {
177 return (
178 <Task id="queue-parse" output={outputs.frcQueue}>
179 {() => {
180 const rows = parseQueueRows(readFileSync(c.queuePath, "utf8"));
181
182 const leafRows = rows.filter((r) => r.scc === "-");
183 const sccRows = rows.filter((r) => r.scc !== "-");
184 const sccSet = new Set(sccRows.map((r) => r.module));
185 const byName = new Map(sccRows.map((r) => [r.module, r]));
186
187 const fail = failQueueContract;
188
189 // Leaves: exactly the 22 scc==="-" rows, in queue order.
190 const inFileOrder = leafRows.every((r, i) => i === 0 || leafRows[i - 1].order < r.order);
191 if (leafRows.length !== 22 || !inFileOrder) {
192 fail(`expected 22 leaf rows in queue order, got leaves=${leafRows.length} ordered=${inFileOrder}`);
193 }
194
195 const leaves: SliceDef[] = leafRows.map((r) => {
196 const id = `m4-leaf-${r.module}`;
197 if (!SAFE_ID.test(id)) fail(`slice id "${id}" must match ${SAFE_ID}`);
198 return {
199 id,
200 kind: "leaf",
201 modules: [r.module],
202 gate: r.gate,
203 };
204 });
205
206 if (sccRows.length !== 59) {
207 fail(`expected one 59-module SCC, got scc=${sccRows.length}`);
208 }
209
210 // Intra-SCC reverse adjacency, for gate inheritance.
211 const dependents = new Map(sccRows.map((r) => [r.module, [] as string[]]));
212 for (const r of sccRows) for (const d of r.deps) if (sccSet.has(d)) dependents.get(d)!.push(r.module);
213
214 /**
215 * A module's gate tests: its own gating_tests, else the top-4 (by
216 * cases) of its transitive intra-SCC dependents — the suites that
217 * actually exercise it. Mirrors the TSV's own top4 convention.
218 */
219 const effectiveTests = (m: string): Array<{ file: string; cases: number }> => {
220 const own = parseGating(byName.get(m)!.gate);
221 if (own.length > 0) return own;
222 const seen = new Set([m]);
223 const queue = [m];
224 const pool = new Map<string, number>();
225 while (queue.length) {
226 const cur = queue.shift()!;
227 for (const dep of dependents.get(cur)!) {
228 if (seen.has(dep)) continue;
229 seen.add(dep);
230 queue.push(dep);
231 for (const t of parseGating(byName.get(dep)!.gate))
232 pool.set(t.file, Math.max(pool.get(t.file) ?? 0, t.cases));
233 }
234 }
235 return [...pool.entries()]
236 .sort((a, b) => b[1] - a[1] || a[0].localeCompare(b[0]))
237 .slice(0, 4)
238 .map(([file, cases]) => ({ file, cases }));
239 };
240
241 // Semantic contract: the COHORTS table must be an exact, bounded,
242 // really-gated partition of the 59 SCC modules.
243 const assignedCount = new Map<string, number>();
244 const testDir = TEST_DIR(c.reactRepo);
245 const cohorts: SliceDef[] = COHORTS.map(([suffix, mods]) => {
246 const id = `m4-cohort-${suffix}`;
247 if (!SAFE_ID.test(id)) fail(`slice id "${id}" must match ${SAFE_ID}`);
248 if (mods.length === 0) fail(`cohort ${id} is empty`);
249 if (mods.length > MAX_COHORT_MODULES) {
250 fail(
251 `cohort m4-cohort-${suffix} has ${mods.length} modules, over MAX_COHORT_MODULES=${MAX_COHORT_MODULES}`,
252 );
253 }
254 let loc = 0;
255 const gatePool = new Map<string, number>();
256 for (const m of mods) {
257 const row =
258 byName.get(m) ?? fail(`cohort m4-cohort-${suffix} names "${m}", which is not an SCC row in the queue`);
259 assignedCount.set(m, (assignedCount.get(m) ?? 0) + 1);
260 loc += row.loc;
261 for (const t of effectiveTests(m)) gatePool.set(t.file, Math.max(gatePool.get(t.file) ?? 0, t.cases));
262 }
263 if (loc > MAX_COHORT_LOC) {
264 fail(`cohort m4-cohort-${suffix} is ${loc} LOC, over MAX_COHORT_LOC=${MAX_COHORT_LOC}`);
265 }
266 if (gatePool.size === 0) {
267 fail(`cohort m4-cohort-${suffix} has an empty derived gate (no own or inheritable gating_tests)`);
268 }
269 const gate = [...gatePool.entries()]
270 .sort((a, b) => b[1] - a[1] || a[0].localeCompare(b[0]))
271 .map(([file, cases]) => `${file}(${cases})`)
272 .join(",");
273 if (gate === BLANKET_GATE) {
274 fail(`cohort m4-cohort-${suffix} is gated on the blanket suite`);
275 }
276 for (const file of gatePool.keys()) {
277 if (!existsSync(join(testDir, file))) {
278 fail(
279 `cohort m4-cohort-${suffix} gate lists ${file}, missing from ${testDir} in the pinned react checkout`,
280 );
281 }
282 }
283 return { id, kind: "cohort" as const, modules: mods, gate };
284 });
285
286 const duplicated = [...assignedCount.entries()].filter(([, n]) => n > 1).map(([m]) => m);
287 const unassigned = sccRows.map((r) => r.module).filter((m) => !assignedCount.has(m));
288 if (assignedCount.size !== 59 || duplicated.length > 0 || unassigned.length > 0) {
289 fail(
290 `COHORTS table must assign all 59 SCC modules exactly once; assigned=${assignedCount.size} duplicated=[${duplicated.join(",")}] unassigned=[${unassigned.join(",")}]`,
291 );
292 }
293
294 return {
295 totalRows: rows.length,
296 leafCount: leaves.length,
297 cohortCount: cohorts.length,
298 sccModules: sccRows.length,
299 slices: JSON.stringify([...leaves, ...cohorts]),
300 };
301 }}
302 </Task>
303 );
304}

One vertical slice: implement in an isolated worktree, two diff-only adversarial reviews from different model families, then the deterministic verifier — looping on one convergence predicate that also gates the right to land.

1/** @jsxImportSource smithers-orchestrator */
2import { Loop, MergeQueue, Parallel, Sequence, Worktree } from "smithers-orchestrator";
3import { Task, outputs } from "./ferricSmithers";
4import { codexReviewerSeatsFor, implementerSeatsFor, opusSeatsFor } from "./ferricAgents";
5import { LANE_ROOT, type FerricConfig, type SliceDef } from "./ferricConfig";
6import { readLedger, writeLedger } from "./ferricLedger";
7import { assertNotInfra, sh } from "./ferricShell";
8import SliceImplementPrompt from "../../prompts/ferric-slice-implement.mdx";
9import SliceReviewPrompt from "../../prompts/ferric-slice-review.mdx";
10
11const CLAUDE_LENS =
12 "Your lens: semantic drift from the TypeScript original, missed DEV-warning parity, and " +
13 "anything that recurses on tree depth. Compare against the upstream sources directly.";
14const CODEX_LENS =
15 "Your lens: ABI and S1–S26 contract violations, reentrancy hazards from E1–E12, ownership " +
16 "and generational-handle misuse, and tests that were narrowed rather than satisfied.";
17
18/**
19 * One vertical slice: implement in an isolated lane, loop implement → two
20 * diff-only adversarial reviews from different model families → deterministic
21 * in-lane verifier, until ONE convergence predicate holds.
22 *
23 * That predicate also gates land admission, which is what makes the verifier's
24 * veto structural: no reviewer and no human approval can route around it.
25 */
26export function Slice(props: { key?: string; ctx: any; c: FerricConfig; slice: SliceDef }) {
27 const { ctx, c, slice } = props;
28 const sid = slice.id;
29 const ledger = readLedger(c.repo);
30 if (ledger.landed.includes(sid)) return null;
31
32 const verify = ctx.latest(outputs.frcVerify, `${sid}:verify`);
33 const revClaude = ctx.latest(outputs.frcReview, `${sid}:review-claude`);
34 const revCodex = ctx.latest(outputs.frcReview, `${sid}:review-codex`);
35 const rounds = ctx.iterationCount(outputs.frcVerify, `${sid}:verify`);
36
37 // Escalation raises the Codex tier for the implementer seat and flips the
38 // Codex reviewer to the opposite tier, so the model that wrote a slice can
39 // never be the model that reviews it.
40 // Per-lane seats: lanes run concurrently, so each takes a different slot in
41 // the account-fleet rotation instead of every lane stacking on the same
42 // "best" account and collapsing its session window.
43 const escalated = rounds >= 2;
44 const implementAgent = implementerSeatsFor(sid, escalated);
45 const codexReviewer = codexReviewerSeatsFor(sid, escalated);
46 const claudeReviewer = opusSeatsFor(sid);
47
48 const converged = verify?.ok === true && revClaude?.approved === true && revCodex?.approved === true;
49
50 const lanePath = `${LANE_ROOT}/${sid}`;
51 const diffCommand = `jj diff --from "fork_point(main | ferric/${sid})" --to ferric/${sid}`;
52 const feedback = [
53 verify && !verify.ok ? `Deterministic verifier VETO (fix these first):\n${verify.reasons}` : "",
54 revClaude && !revClaude.approved ? `Reviewer (claude-opus) blocking findings:\n${revClaude.findings}` : "",
55 revCodex && !revCodex.approved ? `Reviewer (codex) blocking findings:\n${revCodex.findings}` : "",
56 ]
57 .filter(Boolean)
58 .join("\n\n");
59
60 return (
61 <Sequence label={`slice ${sid}`}>
62 <Worktree id={`${sid}:wt`} path={lanePath} branch={`ferric/${sid}`} baseBranch="main">
63 <Loop id={`${sid}:loop`} until={converged} maxIterations={4} onMaxReached="return-last">
64 <Sequence>
65 <Task id={`${sid}:implement`} output={outputs.frcSlice} agent={implementAgent} timeoutMs={7_200_000}>
66 <SliceImplementPrompt
67 sliceId={sid}
68 kind={slice.kind}
69 modules={slice.modules.join(", ")}
70 gate={slice.gate || "the mapped jest cohort"}
71 reactRepo={c.reactRepo}
72 feedback={feedback ? `## Blocking feedback from the previous round\n\n${feedback}` : ""}
73 />
74 </Task>
75 <Parallel label={`${sid} adversarial review`}>
76 <Task
77 id={`${sid}:review-claude`}
78 output={outputs.frcReview}
79 agent={claudeReviewer}
80 continueOnFail
81 timeoutMs={1_800_000}
82 >
83 <SliceReviewPrompt
84 sliceId={sid}
85 reviewer="claude-opus"
86 lens={CLAUDE_LENS}
87 diffCommand={diffCommand}
88 reactRepo={c.reactRepo}
89 />
90 </Task>
91 <Task
92 id={`${sid}:review-codex`}
93 output={outputs.frcReview}
94 agent={codexReviewer}
95 continueOnFail
96 timeoutMs={1_800_000}
97 >
98 <SliceReviewPrompt
99 sliceId={sid}
100 reviewer="codex"
101 lens={CODEX_LENS}
102 diffCommand={diffCommand}
103 reactRepo={c.reactRepo}
104 />
105 </Task>
106 </Parallel>
107 <Task id={`${sid}:verify`} output={outputs.frcVerify} retries={2}>
108 {async () => {
109 // Deterministic verifier: compute, no model, executed in the LANE
110 // worktree. Every step below is exit-coded; a step that cannot run is a
111 // red, never a skip (assertNotInfra still discriminates OOM/timeout).
112 const lane = ctx.worktreePath(`${sid}:wt`) ?? lanePath;
113 const reasons: string[] = [];
114 const diffRange = `fork_point(main | ferric/${sid})`;
115
116 const diff = await sh(["jj", "diff", "--from", diffRange, "--to", `ferric/${sid}`, "--stat"], lane);
117 if (!diff.ok || diff.out.trim().length === 0) {
118 reasons.push("lane has no committed diff vs its fork point");
119 }
120
121 // The patch itself, for the review UI's DiffHunks surface.
122 // Truncated so a large slice cannot bloat the persisted row.
123 const patch = await sh(
124 [
125 "bash",
126 "-lc",
127 'jj diff --from "$1" --to "$2" --git | head -c 200000',
128 "bash",
129 diffRange,
130 `ferric/${sid}`,
131 ],
132 lane,
133 );
134
135 const stubs = await sh(
136 [
137 "bash",
138 "-lc",
139 'jj diff --from "$1" --to "$2" | grep -nE "todo!\\(|unimplemented!\\(" | head -20 || true',
140 "bash",
141 diffRange,
142 `ferric/${sid}`,
143 ],
144 lane,
145 );
146 if (stubs.out.trim()) reasons.push(`stub markers in diff:\n${stubs.out}`);
147
148 // unsafe is permitted only inside the ABI crate (ownership mandate §1).
149 const unsafeGrep = await sh(
150 [
151 "bash",
152 "-lc",
153 'jj diff --from "$1" --to "$2" -- \'glob:**/*.rs\' \'glob:!crates/ferric-abi/**\' | grep -nE "^\\+.*\\bunsafe\\b" | head -20 || true',
154 "bash",
155 diffRange,
156 `ferric/${sid}`,
157 ],
158 lane,
159 );
160 if (unsafeGrep.out.trim()) {
161 reasons.push(`unsafe outside crates/ferric-abi:\n${unsafeGrep.out}`);
162 }
163
164 const check = await sh(["cargo", "check", "--workspace", "--locked"], lane);
165 assertNotInfra(check, "cargo-check");
166 if (!check.ok) reasons.push(`cargo check failed:\n${check.err.slice(-2000)}`);
167
168 const clippy = await sh(
169 ["cargo", "clippy", "--workspace", "--all-targets", "--locked", "--", "-D", "warnings"],
170 lane,
171 );
172 assertNotInfra(clippy, "cargo-clippy");
173 if (!clippy.ok) reasons.push(`clippy failed:\n${clippy.err.slice(-2000)}`);
174
175 const unit = await sh(["cargo", "test", "--workspace", "--locked"], lane);
176 assertNotInfra(unit, "cargo-test");
177 if (!unit.ok) reasons.push(`cargo test failed:\n${unit.err.slice(-2000)}`);
178
179 // D3, mechanically: no engine function recurses on tree/element/child
180 // depth. Engine crates only — diff-ffi test tooling is exempt by path.
181 const recursion = await sh(
182 [
183 "bash",
184 "scripts/ferric/tree-recursion-lint.sh",
185 "crates/ferric-engine",
186 "crates/ferric-lane",
187 "crates/ferric-fiber",
188 ],
189 lane,
190 );
191 assertNotInfra(recursion, "tree-recursion-lint");
192 if (!recursion.ok) {
193 reasons.push(`D3 tree-depth recursion lint:\n${recursion.err.slice(-2000)}`);
194 }
195
196 // FFI differential tier (test-only feature; slices that declare a
197 // differential target must be byte-identical to the pinned JS reference).
198 const hasDiffTarget = await sh(
199 [
200 "bash",
201 "-lc",
202 'jj diff --from "$1" --to "$2" --name-only | grep -q "diff-ffi" && echo yes || true',
203 "bash",
204 diffRange,
205 `ferric/${sid}`,
206 ],
207 lane,
208 );
209 if (hasDiffTarget.out.trim() === "yes") {
210 const ffi = await sh(
211 ["cargo", "test", "--locked", "--features", "diff-ffi", "--test", "differential"],
212 lane,
213 );
214 assertNotInfra(ffi, "diff-ffi");
215 if (!ffi.ok) reasons.push(`FFI differential tier diverged:\n${ffi.err.slice(-2000)}`);
216 }
217
218 // Per-slice DEV-warning parity (only for slices touching warnings.rs).
219 const touchesWarnings = await sh(
220 [
221 "bash",
222 "-lc",
223 'jj diff --from "$1" --to "$2" --name-only | grep -q "warnings.rs" && echo yes || true',
224 "bash",
225 diffRange,
226 `ferric/${sid}`,
227 ],
228 lane,
229 );
230 if (touchesWarnings.out.trim() === "yes") {
231 const parity = await sh(["bash", "scripts/ferric/warnings-parity.sh", sid], lane);
232 assertNotInfra(parity, "warnings-parity");
233 if (!parity.ok) reasons.push(`warning parity check failed:\n${parity.err.slice(-2000)}`);
234 }
235
236 // The slice suite runs under the handle tripwire (FERRIC_HANDLE_TRIPWIRE=1
237 // is set inside slice-suite.sh from M2 onward; the script must print
238 // HANDLE_LEAKS=0 alongside PASSING=n/m).
239 const suite = await sh(["bash", "scripts/ferric/slice-suite.sh", sid], lane);
240 assertNotInfra(suite, "slice-suite");
241 const m = /PASSING=(\d+)\/(\d+)/.exec(suite.out);
242 const passed = m ? Number(m[1]) : 0;
243 const total = m ? Number(m[2]) : 0;
244 if (!suite.ok || !m) {
245 reasons.push(`slice suite not green/parseable:\n${(suite.out || suite.err).slice(-2000)}`);
246 } else if (passed !== total || total === 0) {
247 reasons.push(`slice suite ${passed}/${total} — zero-test runs don't count`);
248 }
249 const leaks = /HANDLE_LEAKS=(\d+)/.exec(suite.out);
250 if (!leaks) {
251 reasons.push("slice suite did not report HANDLE_LEAKS (tripwire not armed)");
252 } else if (Number(leaks[1]) !== 0) {
253 reasons.push(`handle tripwire: HANDLE_LEAKS=${leaks[1]} live handles after teardown`);
254 }
255
256 return {
257 sliceId: sid,
258 ok: reasons.length === 0,
259 testsPassed: passed,
260 testsTotal: total,
261 reasons: reasons.join("\n---\n") || "clean",
262 diffText: patch.out || null,
263 };
264 }}
265 </Task>
266 </Sequence>
267 </Loop>
268 </Worktree>
269
270 {converged && !ledger.halted ? (
271 // Every land task in the campaign mounts under this same explicit id, so
272 // the engine pools them into ONE cap-1 landing queue across all lanes.
273 <MergeQueue id="ferric-land">
274 <Task id={`${sid}:land:e${ledger.haltEpoch}`} output={outputs.frcLand}>
275 {async () => {
276 const led = readLedger(c.repo);
277 if (led.landed.includes(sid)) {
278 return {
279 sliceId: sid,
280 landed: true,
281 regression: false,
282 ratchetBefore: led.passingCount,
283 ratchetAfter: led.passingCount,
284 haltEpoch: led.haltEpoch,
285 };
286 }
287
288 const merge = await sh(
289 [
290 "bash",
291 "-lc",
292 'jj new main "$1" -m "$2" && jj bookmark set main -r @',
293 "bash",
294 `ferric/${sid}`,
295 `[ferric] land ${sid}`,
296 ],
297 c.repo,
298 );
299 if (!merge.ok) throw new Error(`land merge failed for ${sid}:\n${merge.err.slice(-2000)}`);
300
301 // The ratchet is measured AFTER the merge, on the merged tree.
302 const suite = await sh(["bash", "scripts/ferric/oracle.sh", "--ratchet"], c.repo);
303 assertNotInfra(suite, "ratchet");
304 const m = /PASSING=(\d+)\/(\d+)/.exec(suite.out);
305 const after = m ? Number(m[1]) : 0;
306 const total = m ? Number(m[2]) : 0;
307 const regression = !m || after < led.passingCount;
308
309 if (regression) {
310 await sh(["bash", "-lc", "jj bookmark set main -r main- --allow-backwards"], c.repo);
311 writeLedger(c.repo, { ...led, halted: true });
312 return {
313 sliceId: sid,
314 landed: false,
315 regression: true,
316 ratchetBefore: led.passingCount,
317 ratchetAfter: after,
318 haltEpoch: led.haltEpoch,
319 };
320 }
321
322 writeLedger(c.repo, {
323 passingCount: after,
324 totalCount: total,
325 landed: [...led.landed, sid],
326 haltEpoch: led.haltEpoch,
327 halted: false,
328 });
329 return {
330 sliceId: sid,
331 landed: true,
332 regression: false,
333 ratchetBefore: led.passingCount,
334 ratchetAfter: after,
335 haltEpoch: led.haltEpoch,
336 };
337 }}
338 </Task>
339 </MergeQueue>
340 ) : null}
341 </Sequence>
342 );
343}

1/** @jsxImportSource smithers-orchestrator */
2import { Task, outputs } from "./ferricSmithers";
3import { assertNotInfra, sh } from "./ferricShell";
4
5/**
6 * Run one leg of the oracle and persist the measured result.
7 *
8 * A missing or unparseable `PASSING=n/m` line, or a zero denominator, is a red —
9 * never a pass. An audited implementation treated a regex miss plus exit 0 as
10 * green, which let a suite that ran nothing certify a slice.
11 */
12export function SuiteTask(props: { id: string; leg: string; args: string[]; repo: string }) {
13 return (
14 <Task id={props.id} output={outputs.frcSuite} retries={2}>
15 {async () => {
16 const r = await sh(["bash", "scripts/ferric/oracle.sh", ...props.args], props.repo);
17 assertNotInfra(r, props.id);
18 const m = /PASSING=(\d+)\/(\d+)(?:\s+XFAIL_C=(\d+))?/.exec(r.out);
19 const passing = m ? Number(m[1]) : 0;
20 const total = m ? Number(m[2]) : 0;
21 return {
22 leg: props.leg,
23 passingCount: passing,
24 totalCount: total,
25 green: r.ok && !!m && passing === total && total > 0,
26 xfailBucketC: m?.[3] ? Number(m[3]) : 0,
27 };
28 }}
29 </Task>
30 );
31}

1/** @jsxImportSource smithers-orchestrator */
2import type { ReactNode } from "react";
3import { ContinueAsNew, Sequence } from "smithers-orchestrator";
4import { outputs } from "./ferricSmithers";
5import { CampaignGate, gateRow } from "./CampaignGate";
6import { NEXT, type FerricConfig, type Milestone, type SliceDef } from "./ferricConfig";
7import { frontier } from "./ferricLedger";
8import { PortCampaign } from "./PortCampaign";
9import { Closeout } from "./Closeout";
10import type { FerricGateId } from "./ferricGates";
11
12/**
13 * The shared shape of a milestone that is "run the slice machine over a fixed
14 * set, then gate": M1, M2, M5/M6, M7, and M9's implementation half.
15 *
16 * The gate mounts when the frontier is done OR has blocked lanes — never only on
17 * all-green, so an exhausted lane surfaces as evidence at the gate instead of
18 * crashing past it.
19 */
20export function TrialPhase(props: {
21 ctx: any;
22 c: FerricConfig;
23 milestone: Milestone;
24 slices: SliceDef[];
25 gateId: FerricGateId;
26 summary?: string;
27 evidence?: ReactNode;
28 extra?: ReactNode;
29}) {
30 const { ctx, c } = props;
31 const f = frontier(ctx, c.repo, props.slices, outputs);
32 const gateReady = f.done || f.blocked.length > 0;
33 const decided = gateRow(ctx, props.gateId);
34
35 return (
36 <Sequence label={`${props.milestone} phase`}>
37 <PortCampaign ctx={ctx} c={c} phase={props.milestone} slices={props.slices} />
38 {props.extra ?? null}
39 {gateReady ? (props.evidence ?? null) : null}
40 {gateReady ? (
41 <Sequence>
42 <CampaignGate
43 id={props.gateId}
44 summary={`${props.milestone}: ${f.landed.length}/${f.total} slices landed; ratchet ${f.ledger.passingCount}/${f.ledger.totalCount}. Blocked lanes: ${f.blocked.map((b) => b.id).join(", ") || "none"}.${props.summary ? `\n\n${props.summary}` : ""}\n\nEvidence: frcLand, frcVerify, frcReview, and frcSuite rows. Blocked lanes are red evidence — approving with blocked lanes means accepting the documented gap.`}
45 />
46 {decided?.approved ? (
47 <ContinueAsNew
48 state={{
49 milestone: NEXT[props.milestone],
50 spentCents: c.spentCents,
51 lineage: [...c.lineage, ctx.runId],
52 }}
53 />
54 ) : decided?.approved === false ? (
55 // Denial must REACH this branch, which is why exit gates are
56 // onDeny:"continue" rather than "fail": "fail" aborts the run before
57 // the mandated signed closeout can render, so a killed campaign would
58 // end silently instead of publishing its post-mortem.
59 <Closeout
60 ctx={ctx}
61 c={c}
62 reason={`${props.milestone} exit gate denied by the operator: ${f.landed.length}/${f.total} slices landed, blocked lanes: ${f.blocked.map((b) => b.id).join(", ") || "none"}.`}
63 />
64 ) : null}
65 </Sequence>
66 ) : null}
67 </Sequence>
68 );
69}

3/**
4 * Sandwich routing (spec §6): Fable plans and gates, Terra/Sol implement, Opus
5 * reviews, Luna does mechanical work.
6 *
7 * Every seat is an ORDERED FALLBACK CHAIN across the registered account fleet,
8 * not a single agent, for two reasons:
9 *
10 * 1. Load balancing. A campaign this size cannot run on one subscription. The
11 * chain is ordered by live per-account headroom from the usage snapshot
12 * (see ../accounts/accountPool), conserving scarce Fable capacity for the
13 * work only Fable does.
14 * 2. Failover. `agent={[primary, ...fallbacks]}` advances on preflight or
15 * mid-attempt failure, so an account hitting its window costs one hop
16 * instead of parking the run — the failure mode that killed several
17 * multi-hour rounds when every Claude seat pointed at one account.
18 *
19 * The module-level seats below are resolved once per run, which is the right
20 * granularity for a milestone-per-run campaign: each run re-reads the snapshot,
21 * and within a run the chain absorbs quota death. Anything that FANS OUT should
22 * use the per-lane functions instead, so concurrent lanes land on different
23 * accounts rather than stacking on the same one.
24 *
25 * Account binding is `configDir` (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR / CODEX_HOME) and every
26 * Claude seat blanks ANTHROPIC_API_KEY — see ../accounts/accountAgents.
27 */
28
29/* ── singleton seats: stable call sites, resolved once per run ── */
30
31export const fable = claudeSeats("claude-fable-5");
32export const opus = claudeSeats("claude-opus-4-8");
33export const sol = codexSeats("gpt-5.6-sol");
34export const terra = codexSeats("gpt-5.6-terra", "default", "high");
35export const luna = codexSeats("gpt-5.6-luna", "default", "medium");
36
37/** Planning/gating seat: Fable first, Opus behind it. */
38export const planner = [...fable, ...opus];
39
40/** Mechanical seat: cheap tier first, escalating only if the cheap tier dies. */
41export const mechanical = [...luna, ...terra];
42
43/* ── per-lane seats: use these anywhere lanes run concurrently ── */
44
45/** Opus reviewer bound to this lane's slot in the fleet rotation. */
46export const opusSeatsFor = (laneKey: string) => claudeSeats("claude-opus-4-8", laneKey);
47
48/**
49 * Implementer seat. Escalation swaps the Codex TIER order rather than the
50 * family, so the model that implemented a slice is never the one reviewing it.
51 */
52export const implementerSeatsFor = (laneKey: string, escalated: boolean) =>
53 escalated
54 ? [...codexSeats("gpt-5.6-sol", laneKey), ...codexSeats("gpt-5.6-terra", laneKey, "high")]
55 : [...codexSeats("gpt-5.6-terra", laneKey, "high"), ...codexSeats("gpt-5.6-sol", laneKey)];
56
57/** The Codex reviewer tier, opposite whichever tier implemented this round. */
58export const codexReviewerSeatsFor = (laneKey: string, escalated: boolean) =>
59 escalated ? codexSeats("gpt-5.6-terra", laneKey, "high") : codexSeats("gpt-5.6-sol", laneKey);

41export type FerricConfig = {

51/**
52 * Resolve run configuration from input and the ContinueAsNew continuation.
53 *
54 * An unknown milestone throws rather than falling through to a terminal phase:
55 * an audited implementation routed typos to `DONE` and "completed" the campaign
56 * on a misspelling.
57 */
58export function cfg(ctx: any): FerricConfig {
59 const cont = (ctx.input as any)?.__smithersContinuation?.payload ?? {};
60 // The CONTINUATION wins over the launch input. Run input is immutable and is
61 // carried into every successor run, so reading it first pins the campaign to
62 // the milestone it was launched at: M0 hands off to M1, the successor reads
63 // input.milestone === "M0" again, and the campaign loops M0 forever.
64 const rawMilestone = cont.milestone ?? ctx.input?.milestone ?? "M0";
65 if (!MILESTONES.includes(rawMilestone)) {
66 throw new Error(`Unknown milestone "${rawMilestone}". Valid: ${MILESTONES.join(", ")}`);
67 }
68 return {
69 milestone: rawMilestone as Milestone,
70 repo: ctx.input?.campaignRepoPath ?? LAUNCH_ROOT,
71 reactRepo: ctx.input?.reactRepoPath ?? "/Users/williamcory/react",
72 queuePath:
73 ctx.input?.moduleQueuePath ?? "/Users/williamcory/smithers/.smithers/specs/react-rust-port/MODULE_QUEUE.tsv",
74 maxLanes: Math.min(6, Math.max(4, ctx.input?.maxLanes ?? 4)),
75 spentCents: Math.max(ctx.input?.modelSpentCents ?? 0, cont.spentCents ?? 0),
76 lineage: (cont.lineage ?? []) as string[],
77 };
78}

85export const LANE_ROOT = (() => {

1import { existsSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
2import { join } from "node:path";
3import type { SliceDef } from "./ferricConfig";
4
5/**
6 * The durable landing ledger: the campaign's source of truth for what has
7 * actually landed and whether the queue is halted.
8 *
9 * Written ONLY by the land task (sole-writer invariant), read everywhere. It
10 * lives on disk rather than in run state so an operator restart, a fresh
11 * milestone run, or a hand inspection all see the same frontier.
12 */
13export type FerricLedger = {
14 passingCount: number;
15 totalCount: number;
16 landed: string[];
17 haltEpoch: number;
18 halted: boolean;
19};
20
21const EMPTY: FerricLedger = {
22 passingCount: 0,
23 totalCount: 0,
24 landed: [],
25 haltEpoch: 0,
26 halted: false,
27};
28
29export function readLedger(repo: string): FerricLedger {
30 const p = join(repo, "ferric-ledger.json");
31 if (!existsSync(p)) return { ...EMPTY };
32 try {
33 return { ...EMPTY, ...JSON.parse(readFileSync(p, "utf8")) };
34 } catch {
35 // An unreadable ledger is not an empty ledger: halt rather than re-land.
36 return { ...EMPTY, halted: true };
37 }
38}
39
40export function writeLedger(repo: string, ledger: FerricLedger): void {
41 writeFileSync(join(repo, "ferric-ledger.json"), JSON.stringify(ledger, null, 2));
42}
43
44export type Frontier = {
45 ledger: FerricLedger;
46 landed: SliceDef[];
47 blocked: SliceDef[];
48 total: number;
49 done: boolean;
50};
51
52/**
53 * What a milestone gate needs to know: progress, and which lanes gave up.
54 *
55 * Blocked slices are evidence presented AT the gate, not a crash before it — an
56 * audited failure mode was lane exhaustion crashing past the very kill gate that
57 * existed to judge it.
58 */
59export function frontier(ctx: any, repo: string, slices: SliceDef[], outputs: any): Frontier {
60 const ledger = readLedger(repo);
61 const landed = slices.filter((s) => ledger.landed.includes(s.id));
62 const blocked = slices.filter((s) => {
63 if (ledger.landed.includes(s.id)) return false;
64 const rounds = ctx.iterationCount(outputs.frcVerify, `${s.id}:verify`);
65 const v = ctx.latest(outputs.frcVerify, `${s.id}:verify`);
66 return rounds >= 4 && v?.ok !== true;
67 });
68 return {
69 ledger,
70 landed,
71 blocked,
72 total: slices.length,
73 done: landed.length === slices.length && slices.length > 0,
74 };
75}

4/**
5 * Every persisted shape in the Operation Ferric campaign.
6 *
7 * Keys are `frc`-prefixed on purpose: output tables are shared BY NAME across
8 * every workflow in a workspace DB, so a generic key like `review` would
9 * ALTER-extend another workflow's table into a union of both column sets.
10 *
11 * Agent-written schemas carry required min-length / int fields so an empty
12 * repaired `{}` fails validation and the engine's schema-retry loop re-extracts
13 * the agent's real JSON instead of silently persisting an all-null row.
14 */
15export const ferricSchemas = {
16 input: z.object({
17 milestone: z.string().nullish(), // operator override; enum-validated in cfg()
18 campaignRepoPath: z.string().nullish(), // MUST equal the launch root (foundation gate)
19 reactRepoPath: z.string().nullish(), // pinned upstream checkout
20 moduleQueuePath: z.string().nullish(),
21 maxLanes: z.number().int().nullish(), // clamped 4–6
22 modelSpentCents: z.number().int().nullish(), // operator-attested spend top-up
23 }),
24
25 frcFoundation: z.object({
26 launchRootOk: z.boolean(),
27 scriptsOk: z.boolean(),
28 queueOk: z.boolean(),
29 selfAuditOk: z.boolean(),
30 detail: z.string().min(2),
31 }),
32 frcPlan: z.object({
33 milestone: z.string().min(2),
34 planMarkdown: z.string().min(400),
35 workItems: z.string().min(2), // JSON [{id, kind, modules[], gate}]
36 }),
37 frcCanary: z.object({
38 canary: z.string().min(3),
39 ok: z.boolean(),
40 evidence: z.string().min(5),
41 }),
42 frcDocReview: z.object({
43 doc: z.string().min(2),
44 reviewer: z.string().min(3),
45 approved: z.boolean(),
46 findings: z.string().min(10),
47 }),
48 frcOracle: z.object({
49 passingCount: z.number().int(),
50 totalCount: z.number().int(),
51 manifestSha256: z.string().min(16),
52 ok: z.boolean(),
53 }),
54 frcBenchContract: z.object({
55 contractSha256: z.string().min(16),
56 frozen: z.boolean(),
57 }),
58 frcPoc: z.object({
59 ratioX1000: z.number().int(),

1/**
2 * The deterministic layer's shell helpers.
3 *
4 * Everything the campaign treats as *evidence* runs through here: real commands,
5 * asynchronously (never `spawnSync`, which would block the engine's event loop
6 * and starve concurrent agents' heartbeats through a 90-minute oracle run).
7 */
8
9/** The executable contract M0 must author before any slice work is admitted. */
10export const SCRIPTS = [
11 "scripts/ferric/oracle.sh", // --unmodified | --ratchet | --all | --leg <x> → "PASSING=n/m [XFAIL_C=k]"
12 "scripts/ferric/slice-suite.sh", // <sliceId> → "PASSING=n/m"
13 "scripts/ferric/bench.sh", // <name> → "RATIO_X1000=n"
14 "scripts/ferric/fuzz.sh", // <mode> --cases N → "CASES=n DIVERGENCES=m"
15 "scripts/ferric/leaks.sh", // --cycles N --ssr-requests N → exit status
16 "scripts/ferric/publish.sh", // <artifact> <idempotencyKey>
17];
18
19export type ShellResult = {
20 code: number;
21 ok: boolean;
22 out: string;
23 err: string;
24};
25
26export async function sh(cmd: string[], cwd?: string): Promise<ShellResult> {
27 const proc = Bun.spawn(cmd, { cwd, stdout: "pipe", stderr: "pipe" });
28 const [out, err] = await Promise.all([new Response(proc.stdout).text(), new Response(proc.stderr).text()]);
29 const code = await proc.exited;
30 return { code, ok: code === 0, out: out.slice(-8000), err: err.slice(-8000) };
31}
32
33/**
34 * Infra-vs-red discrimination (spec §1.5). An out-of-memory kill or a timeout is
35 * never semantic evidence, so it throws — the task retries with headroom instead
36 * of minting a false red that would halt the queue.
37 */
38export function assertNotInfra(r: ShellResult, what: string): void {
39 const text = `${r.out}\n${r.err}`;
40 if ([124, 137, 143].includes(r.code) || /out of memory|OOM|Killed: 9|ETIMEDOUT/i.test(text)) {
41 throw new Error(`INFRA_RETRY(${what}): exit ${r.code} — retrying with headroom, not a red`);
42 }
43}
44
45export const sha256 = (text: string) => new Bun.CryptoHasher("sha256").update(text).digest("hex");
46

1/** @jsxImportSource smithers-orchestrator */
2import { Task } from "smithers-orchestrator";
3import { z } from "zod";
4import { SNAPSHOT_PATH, writeSnapshot, type AccountUsage } from "./accountPool";
5
6/**
7 * Probe every registered account's live quota and write the snapshot that
8 * render-time seat selection reads.
9 *
10 * Render is synchronous and must never hit the network, so the probe lives in a
11 * compute Task and selection reads its file. Mount this at the START of a phase
12 * so ordering reflects reality rather than whatever was true hours ago.
13 *
14 * The probe never throws: an unreachable account degrades to an `error` entry
15 * and sorts last. A usage endpoint being down is not a reason to stop a
16 * campaign.
17 */
18export const accountUsageSchema = z.object({
19 snapshotPath: z.string().min(4),
20 accountCount: z.number().int(),
21 claudeCount: z.number().int(),
22 codexCount: z.number().int(),
23 summary: z.string().min(2),
24});
25
26/**
27 * `output` is a prop because output schemas must be registered with the host
28 * workflow's `createSmithers()` call — a component cannot invent its own table.
29 * Register `accountUsageSchema` under any key and pass `outputs.<key>` here.
30 */
31export function RefreshAccountUsage({ id = "accounts:refresh", output }: { id?: string; output: unknown }) {
32 return (
33 <Task id={id} output={output as any} retries={1}>
34 {async () => {
35 const { listAccounts } = await import("@smithers-orchestrator/accounts");
36 const { getAccountUsage } = await import("@smithers-orchestrator/usage");
37
38 const accounts = listAccounts();
39 const probed: AccountUsage[] = await Promise.all(
40 accounts.map(async (a: any) => {
41 const base = {
42 label: a.label,
43 provider: a.provider,
44 configDir: a.configDir,
45 model: a.model,
46 };
47 try {
48 const report: any = await getAccountUsage(a);
49 return {
50 ...base,
51 windows: report?.windows ?? [],
52 error: report?.error ?? null,
53 fetchedAt: report?.fetchedAt,
54 };
55 } catch (err) {
56 return {
57 ...base,
58 windows: [],
59 error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err),
60 };
61 }
62 }),
63 );
64
65 writeSnapshot({ fetchedAt: new Date().toISOString(), accounts: probed });
66
67 const claude = probed.filter((p) => p.provider === "claude-code");
68 const codex = probed.filter((p) => p.provider === "codex");
69 const describe = (p: AccountUsage) => {
70 const five = p.windows.find((w) => w.id === "5h")?.usedPercent;
71 return `${p.label}${five == null ? "" : ` ${five}%`}`;
72 };
73 return {
74 snapshotPath: SNAPSHOT_PATH,
75 accountCount: probed.length,
76 claudeCount: claude.length,
77 codexCount: codex.length,
78 summary:
79 `claude[${claude.map(describe).join(", ") || "none"}] ` +
80 `codex[${codex.map(describe).join(", ") || "none"}]`,
81 };
82 }}
83 </Task>
84 );
85}

1import { ClaudeCodeAgent, CodexAgent } from "smithers-orchestrator";
2import {
3 orderClaudeAccounts,
4 orderCodexAccounts,
5 readSnapshot,
6 rotate,
7 type AccountUsage,
8 type ClaudeRole,
9} from "./accountPool";
10
11/**
12 * Build agent FALLBACK CHAINS bound to individual accounts.
13 *
14 * `configDir` is the primitive: it points the vendor CLI at an isolated config
15 * directory (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` / `CODEX_HOME`), which is how several
16 * subscriptions coexist on one machine — one account per directory.
17 *
18 * Every factory returns an ORDERED ARRAY for `agent={[primary, ...fallbacks]}`.
19 * The engine advances down the chain when an agent fails preflight or dies
20 * mid-attempt, so an account hitting its window costs one hop rather than
21 * parking the run for hours.
22 */
23
24/**
25 * Claude CLI seats must not inherit ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: it takes precedence over
26 * the subscription login, so an exhausted API balance fails every seat while
27 * the subscriptions sit unused.
28 */
29const CLAUDE_ENV = { ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: "" };
30
31/** Enough failover to survive a bad account without an absurd preflight walk. */
32const MAX_CHAIN = 4;
33
34function claudeAgentFor(account: AccountUsage, model: string) {
35 return new ClaudeCodeAgent({
36 model,
37 ...(account.configDir ? { configDir: account.configDir } : {}),
38 env: CLAUDE_ENV,
39 permissionMode: "bypassPermissions",
40 dangerouslySkipPermissions: true,
41 });
42}
43
44function codexAgentFor(account: AccountUsage | null, model: string, effort?: string) {
45 return new CodexAgent({
46 model,
47 ...(account?.configDir ? { configDir: account.configDir } : {}),
48 ...(effort ? { config: { model_reasoning_effort: effort } } : {}),
49 sandbox: "danger-full-access",
50 dangerouslyBypassApprovalsAndSandbox: true,
51 skipGitRepoCheck: true,
52 });
53}
54
55const roleFor = (model: string): ClaudeRole =>
56 model.includes("fable") ? "fable" : model.includes("opus") ? "opus" : "other";
57
58/**
59 * Ordered Claude seats for a model.
60 *
61 * `laneKey` spreads concurrent lanes across accounts: without it every lane
62 * rendering in the same frame picks the same best account and collides on its
63 * session window.
64 */
65export function claudeSeats(model: string, laneKey = "default") {
66 const accounts = readSnapshot()?.accounts ?? [];
67 const ordered = rotate(orderClaudeAccounts(accounts, roleFor(model)), laneKey).slice(0, MAX_CHAIN);
68 if (ordered.length === 0) {
69 // No registry yet: fall back to the ambient login so a fresh machine still
70 // runs. `.smithers/scripts/accounts-login.mjs` provisions the fleet.
71 return [
72 new ClaudeCodeAgent({
73 model,
74 env: CLAUDE_ENV,
75 permissionMode: "bypassPermissions",
76 dangerouslySkipPermissions: true,
77 }),
78 ];
79 }
80 return ordered.map((a) => claudeAgentFor(a, model));
81}
82
83/** Ordered Codex seats, spread by session use. */
84export function codexSeats(model: string, laneKey = "default", effort?: string) {
85 const accounts = readSnapshot()?.accounts ?? [];
86 const ordered = rotate(orderCodexAccounts(accounts), laneKey).slice(0, MAX_CHAIN);
87 if (ordered.length === 0) return [codexAgentFor(null, model, effort)];
88 return ordered.map((a) => codexAgentFor(a, model, effort));
89}
90
91/** Which accounts a role would actually use — for gate evidence and logging. */
92export function seatPlan(model: string, laneKey = "default"): string[] {
93 const accounts = readSnapshot()?.accounts ?? [];
94 const ordered = model.startsWith("gpt-")
95 ? orderCodexAccounts(accounts)
96 : orderClaudeAccounts(accounts, roleFor(model));
97 return rotate(ordered, laneKey)
98 .slice(0, MAX_CHAIN)
99 .map((a) => a.label);
100}
