The selection policy. Given a role, order the registered accounts best-first — conserving the scarce model tier for the work only it can do, keeping session-exhausted accounts in the chain in case their window resets, and rotating per lane so concurrent lanes never stack on one account.

1import { existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
2import { homedir } from "node:os";
3import { dirname, join } from "node:path";
4
5/**
6 * Account load balancing for multi-account campaigns.
7 *
8 * Smithers already ships the registry (`~/.smithers/accounts.json`), the
9 * account→env mapping, and per-account usage probes. What it does not ship is a
10 * SELECTION policy, which is what this module is: given a role, return the
11 * registered accounts ordered best-first.
12 *
13 * Selection returns an ORDER, not a winner. Callers feed the ordered list into
14 * `agent={[primary, ...fallbacks]}`, so a stale snapshot or a mid-run quota
15 * death advances to the next account instead of parking the run — the failure
16 * that repeatedly killed multi-hour rounds when every seat was one account.
17 */
18
19export type UsageWindow = {
20 id: string;
21 label?: string;
22 unit?: string;
23 usedPercent?: number;
24 resetsAt?: string;
25};
26
27export type AccountUsage = {
28 label: string;
29 provider: string;
30 configDir?: string;
31 model?: string;
32 windows: UsageWindow[];
33 /** Set when the probe failed; such accounts stay usable but sort last. */
34 error?: string | null;
35 fetchedAt?: string;
36};
37
38export type UsageSnapshot = {
39 fetchedAt: string;
40 accounts: AccountUsage[];
41};
42
43/** Where the refresh task writes, and render reads. */
44export const SNAPSHOT_PATH = join(homedir(), ".smithers", "account-usage.json");
45
46export function writeSnapshot(snapshot: UsageSnapshot, path = SNAPSHOT_PATH): void {
47 mkdirSync(dirname(path), { recursive: true });
48 writeFileSync(path, JSON.stringify(snapshot, null, 2));
49}
50
51/**
52 * Read the snapshot synchronously. Render is synchronous and must never block
53 * on the network, so the probe runs in a compute Task and render reads its
54 * output. A missing snapshot is not an error: selection degrades to registry
55 * order, and the campaign still runs on the ambient login.
56 */
57export function readSnapshot(path = SNAPSHOT_PATH): UsageSnapshot | null {
58 if (!existsSync(path)) return null;
59 try {
60 return JSON.parse(readFileSync(path, "utf8")) as UsageSnapshot;
61 } catch {
62 return null;
63 }
64}
65
66const pct = (u: AccountUsage, id: string): number | undefined => u.windows.find((w) => w.id === id)?.usedPercent;
67
68/** Percent used in a window whose id contains `needle`, if one is published. */
69const pctLike = (u: AccountUsage, needle: string): number | undefined =>
70 u.windows.find((w) => w.id.toLowerCase().includes(needle))?.usedPercent;
71
72/** The rolling session window: the one that actually stops work right now. */
73export const sessionUsed = (u: AccountUsage): number => pct(u, "5h") ?? 0;
74
75/**
76 * Fable headroom for an account, 0–100.
77 *
78 * The subscription usage endpoint publishes per-model weekly windows
79 * (`seven_day_opus`, `seven_day_sonnet`, and a Fable equivalent as tiers land).
80 * When no Fable-specific window exists we fall back to the overall weekly
81 * figure, which is the conservative proxy: it is the pool Fable draws from
82 * either way.
83 */
84export const fableHeadroom = (u: AccountUsage): number => 100 - (pctLike(u, "fable") ?? pct(u, "weekly") ?? 0);
85
86export const opusHeadroom = (u: AccountUsage): number => 100 - (pctLike(u, "opus") ?? pct(u, "weekly") ?? 0);
87
88/** An account with no session capacity cannot take work at all right now. */
89const EXHAUSTED_SESSION = 98;
90
91export type ClaudeRole = "fable" | "opus" | "other";
92
93/**
94 * Fable is the scarce tier, so the default policy CONSERVES it:
95 * - a Fable task takes the account with the MOST Fable headroom;
96 * - an Opus task takes the account with the LEAST Fable headroom that still
97 * has Opus and session capacity, keeping Fable-rich accounts available for
98 * work only Fable can do.
99 *
100 * Set this to false to make Opus prefer the healthiest account instead. That is
101 * the entire switch, deliberately one constant.
102 */
103export const CONSERVE_FABLE = true;
104
105export function orderClaudeAccounts(accounts: AccountUsage[], role: ClaudeRole): AccountUsage[] {
106 const claude = accounts.filter((a) => a.provider === "claude-code");
107 const usable = claude.filter((a) => sessionUsed(a) < EXHAUSTED_SESSION);
108 const spent = claude.filter((a) => sessionUsed(a) >= EXHAUSTED_SESSION);
109
110 const scored = [...usable].sort((a, b) => {
111 if (role === "fable") {
112 const d = fableHeadroom(b) - fableHeadroom(a); // most Fable first
113 if (d !== 0) return d;
114 } else if (role === "opus" && CONSERVE_FABLE) {
115 // Least Fable headroom first — but an Opus-exhausted account is no use
116 // for an Opus task however much Fable it has left, so that dominates.
117 const oa = opusHeadroom(a);
118 const ob = opusHeadroom(b);
119 if (oa <= 2 || ob <= 2) {
120 const d = ob - oa;
121 if (d !== 0) return d;
122 }
123 const d = fableHeadroom(a) - fableHeadroom(b);
124 if (d !== 0) return d;
125 } else {
126 const d = opusHeadroom(b) - opusHeadroom(a);
127 if (d !== 0) return d;
128 }
129 // Tie-break on the session window so load spreads rather than stacking.
130 const s = sessionUsed(a) - sessionUsed(b);
131 if (s !== 0) return s;
132 return a.label.localeCompare(b.label);
133 });
134
135 // Exhausted accounts stay in the chain, last: a window reset during a long
136 // run makes them viable again, and an empty chain is worse than a tail entry.
137 return [...scored, ...spent];
138}
139
140/** Codex has no tier scarcity: spread by session use, then weekly. */
141export function orderCodexAccounts(accounts: AccountUsage[]): AccountUsage[] {
142 return accounts
143 .filter((a) => a.provider === "codex")
144 .sort((a, b) => {
145 const s = sessionUsed(a) - sessionUsed(b);
146 if (s !== 0) return s;
147 const w = (pct(a, "weekly") ?? 0) - (pct(b, "weekly") ?? 0);
148 if (w !== 0) return w;
149 return a.label.localeCompare(b.label);
150 });
151}
152
153/**
154 * A stable per-lane rotation offset.
155 *
156 * Lanes rendering in the same frame see the same snapshot and would otherwise
157 * all pick the same "best" account and collide on its session window. Rotating
158 * by a lane-derived offset spreads them deterministically — stable across
159 * resume, unlike a counter or a random pick.
160 */
161export function rotate<T>(items: T[], key: string): T[] {
162 if (items.length <= 1) return items;
163 let h = 0;
164 for (const ch of key) h = (h * 31 + ch.charCodeAt(0)) >>> 0;
165 const n = h % items.length;
166 return [...items.slice(n), ...items.slice(0, n)];
167}

1#!/usr/bin/env node
2/**
3 * Provision and log in the account fleet: 8 Claude subscriptions + 2 Codex.
4 *
5 * Each account is an isolated CLI config directory under
6 * `~/.smithers/accounts/<label>`. Pointing the vendor CLI at one via
7 * CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR / CODEX_HOME is the primitive that lets several
8 * subscriptions coexist on one machine; this script drives it in bulk and
9 * registers the result in `~/.smithers/accounts.json`.
10 *
11 * Verified on macOS with Claude Code 2.1.220: setting CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR at all
12 * switches Claude to a config-dir-scoped credential store, separate from the
13 * default `Claude Code-credentials` Keychain item. Pointing CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR at
14 * `~/.claude` — the very directory the ambient login uses — still reports
15 * `loggedIn: false`, which is how we know the scoping is by the setting rather
16 * than by path. Two consequences: every seat needs its own OAuth (the ambient
17 * login cannot be adopted as one of them), and the fleet cannot clobber the
18 * user's existing login.
19 *
20 * Login is the vendor's own browser OAuth flow, which needs a human, so this is
21 * interactive by design. Accounts that are already signed in are skipped, so
22 * re-running is cheap and safe.
23 *
24 * node .smithers/scripts/accounts-login.mjs # provision + log in
25 * node .smithers/scripts/accounts-login.mjs --status # report only
26 * node .smithers/scripts/accounts-login.mjs --claude 8 --codex 2
27 */
28import { spawnSync } from "node:child_process";
29import { mkdirSync } from "node:fs";
30import { homedir } from "node:os";
31import { join } from "node:path";
32
33const args = process.argv.slice(2);
34const flag = (name, dflt) => {
35 const i = args.indexOf(`--${name}`);
36 return i >= 0 && args[i + 1] && !args[i + 1].startsWith("--") ? args[i + 1] : dflt;
37};
38const CLAUDE_N = Number(flag("claude", "8"));
39const CODEX_N = Number(flag("codex", "2"));
40const STATUS_ONLY = args.includes("--status");
41
42const ACCOUNTS_ROOT = join(homedir(), ".smithers", "accounts");
43
44/**
45 * ANTHROPIC_API_KEY takes precedence over the subscription OAuth this fleet is
46 * built on. Left set, `auth status` reports the API key's identity instead of
47 * the account's and `auth login` signs into the wrong thing, so every vendor
48 * call below blanks it.
49 */
50const noApiKey = { ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: "" };
51
52const run = (cmd, cmdArgs, env) => spawnSync(cmd, cmdArgs, { encoding: "utf8", env: { ...process.env, ...env } });
53
54const PROVIDERS = {
55 "claude-code": {
56 labels: Array.from({ length: CLAUDE_N }, (_, i) => `claude-${i + 1}`),
57 env: (dir) => ({ CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR: dir, ...noApiKey }),
58 envName: "CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR",
59 /**
60 * `claude auth status --json` is the authoritative check: it costs no
61 * tokens and reports the identity behind this config dir. Sniffing the
62 * directory for files does NOT work — merely running claude once populates
63 * `.claude.json`, `projects/`, and friends without any login happening.
64 */
65 status(dir) {
66 const r = run("claude", ["auth", "status", "--json"], this.env(dir));
67 try {
68 const j = JSON.parse(r.stdout);
69 return {
70 loggedIn: Boolean(j.loggedIn),
71 identity: j.email ?? null,
72 detail: j.subscriptionType ? `${j.subscriptionType}` : (j.authMethod ?? null),
73 };
74 } catch {
75 return { loggedIn: false, identity: null, detail: null };
76 }
77 },
78 // --claudeai signs into the Claude subscription (not Console API billing),
79 // which is the whole point of running a fleet of them.
80 login: ["claude", ["auth", "login", "--claudeai"]],
81 },
82 codex: {
83 labels: Array.from({ length: CODEX_N }, (_, i) => `codex-acct-${i + 1}`),
84 env: (dir) => ({ CODEX_HOME: dir }),
85 envName: "CODEX_HOME",
86 status(dir) {
87 const r = run("codex", ["login", "status"], this.env(dir));
88 const out = `${r.stdout}${r.stderr}`;
89 const loggedIn = /logged in/i.test(out) && !/not logged in/i.test(out);
90 const identity = out.match(/logged in using ([^\n]+)/i)?.[1]?.trim() ?? null;
91 return { loggedIn, identity, detail: null };
92 },
93 login: ["codex", ["login"]],
94 },
95};
96
97const registered = (() => {
98 const r = run("smithers", ["agents", "list", "--format", "json"], {});
99 try {
100 const parsed = JSON.parse(r.stdout);
101 const rows = parsed?.data?.accounts ?? parsed?.accounts ?? parsed?.data ?? [];
102 return new Set((Array.isArray(rows) ? rows : []).map((a) => a.label));
103 } catch {
104 return new Set();
105 }
106})();
107
108const plan = [];
109for (const [provider, spec] of Object.entries(PROVIDERS)) {
110 for (const label of spec.labels) {
111 const dir = join(ACCOUNTS_ROOT, label);
112 mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
113 plan.push({ provider, label, dir, spec, ...spec.status(dir), registered: registered.has(label) });
114 }
115}
116
117const mark = (b) => (b ? "✓" : "·");
118
119function report() {
120 console.log(`\nAccount fleet — ${CLAUDE_N} claude + ${CODEX_N} codex\n`);
121 for (const p of plan) {
122 const who = p.identity ? `${p.identity}${p.detail ? ` (${p.detail})` : ""}` : "—";
123 console.log(` ${mark(p.loggedIn)} login ${mark(p.registered)} registered ${p.label.padEnd(14)} ${who}`);
124 }
125 const inCount = plan.filter((p) => p.loggedIn).length;
126 console.log(
127 `\n${inCount}/${plan.length} logged in, ` + `${plan.filter((p) => p.registered).length}/${plan.length} registered.`,
128 );
129
130 // A fleet of eight seats all pointing at one subscription has one quota and
131 // buys nothing, so surface it loudly rather than letting it look healthy.
132 const seen = new Map();
133 for (const p of plan) {
134 if (!p.loggedIn || !p.identity) continue;
135 const key = `${p.provider}:${p.identity}`;
136 seen.set(key, [...(seen.get(key) ?? []), p.label]);
137 }
138 const dupes = [...seen.entries()].filter(([, labels]) => labels.length > 1);
139 if (dupes.length > 0) {
140 console.log(`\n ⚠ SHARED SUBSCRIPTIONS — these seats draw from one quota:`);
141 for (const [key, labels] of dupes) {
142 console.log(` ${key.split(":").slice(1).join(":")} → ${labels.join(", ")}`);
143 }
144 console.log(` Log those labels out and back in with different accounts.`);
145 }
146 console.log("");
147}
148
149report();
150if (STATUS_ONLY) process.exit(0);
151
152const missing = plan.filter((p) => !p.loggedIn);
153if (missing.length > 0) {
154 console.log(
155 `${missing.length} account(s) need a browser sign-in. Each opens your browser with an\n` +
156 `isolated config dir; complete the OAuth flow and it moves on to the next.\n\n` +
157 `Sign in with a DIFFERENT subscription for each label — otherwise they all share\n` +
158 `one quota and the fleet buys nothing.\n`,
159 );
160}
161
162for (const p of missing) {
163 const [cmd, cmdArgs] = p.spec.login;
164 console.log(`\n── ${p.label} ─────────────────────────────────────────────`);
165 console.log(` ${cmd} ${cmdArgs.join(" ")} (${p.spec.envName}=${p.dir})`);
166 const r = spawnSync(cmd, cmdArgs, {
167 stdio: "inherit",
168 env: { ...process.env, ...p.spec.env(p.dir) },
169 });
170 if (r.error) {
171 console.log(` ! could not launch ${cmd}: ${r.error.message}`);
172 continue;
173 }
174 const after = p.spec.status(p.dir);
175 Object.assign(p, after);
176 console.log(p.loggedIn ? ` ✓ signed in as ${p.identity ?? "(unknown)"}` : " · still not signed in");
177}
178
179for (const p of plan) {
180 if (!p.loggedIn || p.registered) continue;
181 const r = run(
182 "smithers",
183 ["agents", "add", "--provider", p.provider, "--label", p.label, "--config-dir", p.dir, "--replace"],
184 {},
185 );
186 if (r.status === 0) {
187 p.registered = true;
188 console.log(` ✓ registered ${p.label}`);
189 } else {
190 console.log(` ! register ${p.label} failed: ${(r.stderr || r.stdout || "").trim().split("\n")[0]}`);
191 }
192}
193
194report();
195console.log(`Next: \`smithers usage\` shows per-account headroom; the campaign's`);
196console.log(`accounts:refresh task snapshots it for load-balanced seat selection.\n`);
197

1## Adversarial diff-only review
2
3You are reviewing slice {props.sliceId}. Assume it is wrong and find out why. A review that
4says "looks good" has failed; your job is to produce findings.
5
6Start from the diff, and read only what you need beyond it to judge the diff. Get it with:
7
8{props.diffCommand}
9
10The pinned upstream React checkout is at {props.reactRepo} — read the original of anything this
11diff claims to port. You are not reviewing the whole repository, but a port cannot be judged without
12the source it was ported from, and semantic drift is the primary thing you are here to catch.
13
14{props.lens}

16## What blocks
17
18Only critical and major findings block a landing. Nitpicks, style preferences, and
19"could be cleaner" do not — a review loop that blocks on taste becomes a denial of service
20and the campaign has a hard round cap.
21
22A blocking finding must name the violated invariant or its semantic equivalent, the file and
23line, a concrete failure scenario, and a proposed reproduction. Generic disapproval does not
24count as a finding.
25
26Reject on sight: stubs and `todo!()`, semantic drift from the TypeScript original, recursion
27on tree depth, mismatched DEV warning text, edits to tests or config that change what is
28being measured, and any fallback path back into the JavaScript implementation.
29
30You are identified in your output as {props.reviewer}.
